title: Indian  central bank 's rupee management undermines hedging push
text:
MUMBAI, April 21 (Reuters) - The Reserve Bank of India's intervention to temper the rupee's rise is inflating foreign exchange hedging costs, impeding its own efforts to bolster Corporate India's defenses against potential currency turbulence.

For long, one of the biggest concerns for the RBI has been the risk of a destabilising outflow of funds as the U.S. Federal Reserve edges closer towards raising interest rates from historic lows.

However, it is the rush of foreign money coming into Asia's third-biggest economy - about $14.3 billion has flowed into debt and equity markets this year - that is putting the central bank in a tight spot, forcing it to buy dollars in the spot market and sell them in the forward market.

The effect of removing excess rupees from the system as the RBI sterilises the inflationary effect of money supply has further driven up rupee interest rates above dollar rates. This means banks and companies have to pay more rupees to hedge their dollar liabilities in the futures markets.

Ashish Vaidya, head of trading, asset liability management at DBS in Mumbai, said the RBI has to walk a fine line as it looks to ensure price stability while taking the upward pressure off the rupee from capital inflows.

"The RBI is buying dollars in the spot market and then paying forward to remove the surge of rupee liquidity, as it has to maintain price stability," he said.

Corporates must now pay upwards of 7.6 percent to buy dollars and sell rupees to meet future obligations. The 6-month forward premium on the dollar versus the rupee has risen by around 35 basis points so far in 2015.

"The implication of higher forward dollar/rupee premium is importers are hedging less than they should, which is a risk to the banking system," said Anindya Das Gupta, managing director, head of trading at Barclays in India - precisely the kind of risk the RBI wants to minimise.

Underscoring the perils of inadequate hedging, the rupee fell 0.9 percent intraday on Monday - its steepest slide since Dec 16.

Last October, RBI Deputy Governor H.R. Khan warned the hedge ratio for overseas loans and foreign convertible debt had halved to around 15 percent in July-August from the previous fiscal year.

CAPITAL FLOWS

The rupee was the third best performing currency in Asia in the March quarter, rising 0.85 percent - backed by rising inflows on optimism over economic growth, stable inflation and structural reforms. It has retreated since then and is up around 0.2 percent so far in 2015.

The robust capital inflows have boosted importers' confidence that any rupee depreciation will be less costly than a hedge, while most exporters have also been lax about hedging on the view the currency will move in a tight band.

"If we hedge, we will lose a lot of money," a senior official at a state-run oil company said, noting the short import payments period.

The stubbornly strong rupee has ramped up RBI's operations in the spot forex market - it bought a net $20 billion in January and February. The central bank has also been swapping rupees for dollars in the forward market, adding $260 million in up to one-year dollar contracts in February. In contrast, the RBI's net dollar holdings in tenors up to one-year fell sharply by $6.49 billion in December.

"We are not going to maintain any particular level for the rupee and so they (firms) have to recognize that they are taking on a big risk," Governor Raghuram Rajan said earlier this month, sounding a warning to firms that aren't hedging their currency exposure. (Reporting by Suvashree Choudhury; Editing by Nachum Kaplan and Shri Navaratnam)

title: RPT-India's record  FX  warchest set for Fed rate hike test
text:
(Repeats Thursday story with no changes)

* RBI builds up record forex reserves of $338 billion

* Looming U.S. rate hike could prompt emerging market sell-off

* RBI reserves considered enough to cushion India -source

* India chastened by capital flight in 2013 "taper tantrum"

By Suvashree Choudhury and Swati Bhat

MUMBAI, March 19 (Reuters) - Chastened by a tumble in the rupee in 2013 at the prospect of tighter U.S. monetary policy, India has built up record foreign exchange reserves of nearly $340 billion to insulate the economy from capital flight as the United States prepares to lift interest rates.

Reserve Bank of India Governor Raghuram Rajan has long warned of the risk to emerging economies when the U.S. Federal Reserve makes the first rise in its zero percent interest rates since the 2008 financial crisis.

He has also been actively buying dollars, helped by a net inflow of $54 billion of foreign money since the start of 2014, which has driven shares to record highs and pushed bond yields sharply lower.

The central bank's intervention has seen reserves rise by about a quarter since the end of 2013 to $338 billion and headed off a sharp appreciation in the rupee. That gives him the firepower to limit a slide in the rupee and any dislocation in domestic markets if foreign money rushes out.

"As of now, we have accumulated enough reserves," said a policy maker familiar with the RBI's thinking.

"The Governor has created that space to face a U.S. rate hike," he added. "Adding to reserves was an objective last year. This year it is more to contain volatility."

Those preparations look set to be tested in the coming months after the Fed removed a reference to being "patient" on interest rates from its policy statement on Wednesday, paving the way for a hike within months, though it also signalled it was in no rush to push borrowing costs higher.

In 2013, when he was an economic adviser to the Indian finance ministry, Rajan witnessed firsthand the perils of being unprepared, when concerns about the Fed scaling back its monetary stimulus sparked a "taper tantrum" that roiled emerging markets, saddling India with its worst market turmoil in more than two decades.

India's central bank and finance ministry were seen by markets as unprepared and hesitant in their initial reaction.

Rajan, formerly chief economist at the International Monetary Fund, was credited with a key role in rescuing India from that crisis with measures that helped stem foreign selling.

Rajan said on Wednesday India now had "comfortable" FX reserves and its current account deficit was under control.

INDIA SHINING

India has seen a resurgence in investor popularity since the election of a reform-minded government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, helped by improving economic fundamentals and the RBI's efforts to curb inflation.

It also imposed curbs on gold imports in 2013, a measure that, combined with the slump in crude prices, helped substantially narrow the country's current account deficit.

India has subsequently attracted more foreign capital than the "Fragile Five" countries to which it is often compared, but the RBI considers such inflows a double-edged sword, since they leave it at the whim of global investors

India saw net foreign investments of nearly $20 billion in 2007, ahead of the global financial crisis, only to see investors pull out $9.4 billion the next year.

And in 2013, $8 billion flowed out of its debt markets, sending the rupee to a record low of 68.85 per dollar in August.

As a result, Rajan has pushed hard to build up currency reserves, which had fallen as low as $274.8 billion in September 2013, enough to account for just under seven months of imports, the lowest import cover since 1996.

With the rupee about 10 percent above the 2013 low, the governor can keep adding to those reserves by buying dollars, analysts say.

"The RBI enjoys pretty decent headroom in terms of the intervention they can do," said Siddhartha Sanyal, chief India economist for Barclays. (Writing by Rafael Nam; Editing by Will Waterman)

    By Jongwoo Cheon
    SINGAPORE, March 6 (Reuters) - Most emerging Asian
currencies edged up on Friday to recover some of their weekly
losses as traders covered short positions ahead of U.S. jobs
data later in the day.
    South Korea's won outperformed on demand from
exporters for settlements and bond inflows. The Taiwan dollar
 rose on foreign stock inflows and exporters' bids.

February due later in the day. Analysts polled by Reuters expect
payrolls to have increased 240,000 last month and the jobless
rate to have ticked down to 5.6 percent from 5.7 percent.
 
    Higher-than-expected U.S. jobs data would increase
expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates
earlier, analysts and traders said.
    "A solid jobs number will lift U.S. bond yields and the
dollar. That will definitely hurt Asian currencies," said Jeong
My-young, Samsung Futures' research head in Seoul, referring to
growth in U.S. jobs of more than 240,000.
    "Such expectations, however, have been priced in pretty
much. So, any disappointment will help Asian currencies
rebound," Jeong added.
    Most emerging Asian currencies have already fallen so far
this week as interest rate cuts by China and India spurred
prospects of regional easing.
    Sentiment towards regional units deteriorated in the last
two weeks with short positions in the yuan at a near
five-year high, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.
 
    
    RINGGIT UNDERPERFORMS
    For this week, the Malaysian ringgit led losses
among emerging Asian currencies with a 1.2 percent slide against
the dollar, Thomson Reuters data showed.
    The currency came under pressure on concerns over slowing
growth. Malaysia's exports in January fell 0.6 percent from a
year earlier, missing a 3.0 percent growth forecast.
 
    "We still expect ringgit weakness to persist on a
combination of factors including strong USD trend, soft oil
prices for an extended period, vulnerability to foreign fund
outflow and heightened risk of rating downgrade following
contingent liability exposure, lower fiscal revenue," Maybank
said in a client note.
    Currency traders have not reacted to news that the country's
indebted and controversy-ridden state investor 1MDB will be left
as a skeletal structure and possibly dissolved under a debt
repayment plan in which most of its assets will be sold.
 
    Traders also ignored the central bank's decision on Thursday
to leave interest rates unchanged, as that was widely expected.

was suspected of intervening to stem its appreciation. The

rate by 25 basis points to 7.5 percent, its second
cut outside of a scheduled meeting this year.

rupiah on Thursday fell below psychological support of 13,000
per dollar for the first time since the 1997-98 Asian financial
crisis, as the central bank said a weaker rupiah helps export
competitiveness improve.
    Thailand's baht has eased 0.3 percent, while the
Philippine peso edged weaker.
    By contrast, the yuan has gained 0.1 percent as some

"From a structural point of view, we find it a shame that RRR cuts are seen by some as politically incorrect--an indicator of turning on the monetary taps. (Ranges are calculated using recent highs and lows, information on the placement of option strikes, and technical analysis--Bollinger Bands, Fibonacci levels, trendlines and moving averages.)

USD/CNY--uptrend may end. Spot USD/CNY may slide after the liquidity-boosting move announced by the People's Bank of China late Wednesday. A Thursday close below 6.2482 would affirm that the Bollinger uptrend channel is no longer in play and could lead to capitulation of long-USD positions. The PBOC's 50 basis-point cut in the Reserve Requirement Ratio -- that dictates how much banks need to hold in cash reserves -- ought to boost risk appetite and lift the yuan, thereby weighing on USD/CNY. But the overnight rebound of the U.S. dollar index could result in a stable or higher daily USD/CNY benchmark rate -- which typically exerts influence on spot USD/CNY. The Shanghai stock market is likely to rally significantly with the policy-easing move by the PBOC. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for spot USD/CNY is at 6.2482 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 6.2254 (20-day Bollinger mid support). Immediate resistance is at 6.2500 (psychological resistance), then at 6.2710 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 6.2719 (top of monthly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/TWD--consolidation higher. USD/TWD may rise above the 31.530 ceiling of the daily Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone that coincides with the 20-day Bollinger mid resistance line. A daily close above that mark could lead to near-term consolidation within an elevated range. Overnight U.S. dollar index strength -- due to the euro sinking after the European Central Bank tightened the screws on Greece -- propelled the greenback broadly higher. But risk aversion triggered by Greek uncertainties may be mitigated by the easing measures announced by the People's Bank of China late Wednesday which ought to boost regional equity markets. The price difference between the 1-month USD/TWD nondeliverable forward contract and the spot contract remains at a premium, suggesting that the speculative trading community is mildly bullish on the U.S. dollar. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 31.310 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 31.090 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support). Immediate resistance is likely at 31.530 (top of daily Ichimoku Cloud resistance and 20-day Bollinger mid resistance), then at 31.750 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 31.980 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/KRW--consolidation higher. USD/KRW gapped back up Thursday in reaction to risk aversion bubbling in Europe after the European Central Bank removed a waiver that had allowed Greece access to funding by selling its junk-rated government bonds. The resulting slump in EUR/USD lifted the U.S. dollar index, which is now boosting most USD/Asia pairs. USD/KRW could take on a bullish bias if it ends the day inside the Bollinger uptrend channel that begins at 1,093. But a clean break of the Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone at 1,098 is needed to clear the path for a bigger rally. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 1,087 (20-day Bollinger mid support), then at 1,084 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support), before 1,080 (round-figure trading barrier). Immediate resistance is at 1,090 (round-figure trading barrier), then at 1,093 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 1,098 (top of daily Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone).

USD/SGD--uptrend may return. USD/SGD could climb back into the daily Bollinger uptrend channel as the benchmark U.S. dollar index rebounded sharply overnight on fresh Greek uncertainties. The USD/SGD pair may resume a short-term bullish technical bias if it ends Thursday above 1.3492. The euro sank overnight after the European Central Bank lifted a waiver that allowed Greece to sell its junk-rated bonds to investors, thus pushing the U.S. dollar index higher. The after-market hours announcement of liquidity-easing by the People's Bank of China on Wednesday seemed to have had little effect on external markets -- the Australia dollar blipped higher but then retreated soon after. This could be a sign that Asian stock markets might shrug at China's latest attempt to shore up economic growth. Dow Jones technical analysis shows immediate support is at 1.3405 (20-day Bollinger mid support), then at 1.3400 (round-figure trading barrier), before 1.3319 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 1.3492 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 1.3500 (round-figure trading barrier), before 1.3577 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/MYR--consolidation higher. USD/MYR rebounds sharply at Thursday's open as the ringgit collapses in reaction to the 9% fall in crude-oil prices overnight -- just a day after oil prices had rallied sharply. The reason was apparently a report showing that U.S. oil output hasn't subsided; production cuts by shale oil-drilling companies have likely not shown up in data. An underlying reason for USD/MYR strength was the overnight slump of the euro after the European Central Bank removed an avenue of funding for Greek banks by lifting the waiver that allowed the sale of its junk-rated government bonds. The euro's slide boosted the benchmark U.S. dollar index -- which is lifting most USD/Asia pairs Thursday. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 3.5700 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 3.5500 (psychological support), before 3.5450 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 3.5960 (20-day Bollinger mid resistance), then at 3.6000 (round-figure trading barrier), before 3.6210 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/THB--consolidation higher. USD/THB has been stable recently -- on suspected intervention by the Bank of Thailand to cap baht strength -- but may consolidate higher within the daily Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone after an overnight surge of the benchmark U.S. dollar index. Wednesday's steep drop in EUR/USD -- triggered by the European Central Bank tightening the screws on Greece -- rallied the U.S. dollar index. If USD/THB ends the day above 32.65 -- where the daily Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone coincides with the 20-day Bollinger mid resistance -- consolidation within a range of 32.65-32.76 is likely in the near term. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 32.55 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 32.46 (200-day moving average), before 32.45 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 32.65 (daily Ichimoku Cloud resistance and 20-day Bollinger mid resistance), then at 32.76 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 32.86 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/PHP--consolidation higher. USD/PHP may rise toward the 200-day moving average resistance line at 44.25 as the greenback rallies broadly following a steep retreat in EUR/USD overnight and accompanying risk aversion. The European Central Bank disallowing the sale of junk-rated government bonds by Greece sent shivers into the market, resulting in a weaker euro and a selloff in U.S. stocks. The rebound of the U.S. dollar index and deterioration in risk appetite is lifting most USD/Asia pairs Thursday but a glimmer of hope may come from the Chinese stock market. Shanghai is expected to rally after the People's Bank of China on Wednesday after market hours announced a significant cut in its bank reserves requirement ratio -- an attempt to increase lending to boost the economy. Immediate resistance is likely at 44.10 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 44.25 (200-day moving average), before 44.50 (psychological resistance).

USD/IDR might bounce off the daily Ichimoku Cloud support zone and head back into the daily Bollinger uptrend channel -- thereby reinstating a bullish technical bias -- as the U.S. dollar index rebounded sharply overnight due to the euro's slump. Risk aversion is back on the cards for European investors after the European Central Bank lifted a waiver that allowed Greece to sell its junk-rated government bonds. The resulting drop in the euro has sent traders scurrying back to the safety of the U.S. dollar. USD/Asia has risen broadly in response to the overnight move but risk appetite may be helped by China's announcement of liquidity-easing measures late Wednesday. The somewhat unexpected move by the People's Bank of China ought to lift stocks and lend support to risk-sensitive emerging-market currencies. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for spot USD/IDR is at 12,580 (20-day Bollinger mid support and daily Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 12,500 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 12,440 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support). USD/INR--consolidation higher. USD/INR may rise toward the daily Bollinger uptrend channel as the greenback rallies broadly after an overnight collapse of the euro. Wednesday's announcement by the European Central Bank, which now makes it impossible for Greece to sell its junk-rated government bonds, sent investors away from the euro and to the U.S. dollar. The overnight spike of the benchmark U.S. dollar index has lifted most USD/Asia pairs Thursday but there may be reprieve from China where stocks are expected to rally sharply after the People's Bank of China announced a cut in its banks' reserve requirement ratio -- a move to promote lending to stimulate the economy. But despite recently tumultuous global financial markets, sharp moves for the rupee are unlikely in the near term since the Reserve Bank of India has said it has been intervening in the spot market to reduce rupee volatility. title: Reliance Stock Recovering on $750 Million Bond Issue -- Market Talk
text:
0512 GMT [Dow Jones ] Reliance Industries (500325.BY) stock is recovering from early losses to trade up 0.1% at 938.15 rupees a share after it said Wednesday it had issued bonds worth $750 million, paying an interest of 4.875%. The stock had earlier fallen to 932.20 rupees in early trade Wednesday. Reliance is due to buy these bonds back in 2045. The oil and gas major is paying the lowest interest rate ever paid by an Asian private corporate issuer for a 30-year issuance, Reliance said. Market headline was corrected at 0540 GMT. The original incorrectly stated the issuance as $750.

The outlook for revenues from Australian liquefied natural gas, and bulk commodities shipments--which account for almost half of total export earnings--has deteriorated significantly, it said. Tim Toohey, chief economist at Goldman Sachs said overall export revenues are still forecast to increase over the coming years--underpinned by a strong outlook for physical shipments, particularly for gas. title: India: 895.6 Million Cellphone Users by 2019, Says Cisco -- Market Talk
text:
0633 GMT [Dow Jones] Cisco Systems Inc. (CSCO) forecasts that India will have 895.6 million cellphone users by 2019 up from 590.3 million in 2014. "The number of smartphones will grow 4.7-fold between 2014 and 2019 reaching 651 million," according to Cisco Visual Networking Index™ Global Mobile Data Traffic Forecast for 2014 to 2019, report. The world's biggest networking company further said that internet traffic from cellphones would increase 13-fold, growing at about 67% annually between 2014 and 2019. About 51% of cellular subscriptions in 2019 would be smartphones, up from 8% in 2014; while video will be 66% of cellphone internet traffic by 2019 up from 26% last year, Cisco's report said. (krishna.jai@wsj.com; Twitter: @jaikrishna) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0625 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/JPY may test 119 later this week if diminished risk aversion combines with upbeat U.S. jobs data, says Takuya Kanda, senior researcher at Gaitame.Com Research Institute. "The risk-averse mood has become more relaxed," he says, but improved sentiment -- especially given receding fears over Greece -- have caused the euro to rise against both the dollar and yen, causing a "tug-of-war" between a weaker dollar and weaker yen, thus limiting upward pressure on the USD/JPY. He adds that the current market mood doesn't give a clear direction to the dollar against the yen, and investors may have to wait for U.S. jobs data scheduled for Friday. The USD/JPY is now at 117.64. (hiroyuki.kachi@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: PAB 
 

0623 GMT [Dow Jones] The Commonwealth Bank of Australia has lowered its forecast for the New Zealand dollar to US$0.6800 by end-2015 from US$0.7300. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand has moved from a tightening bias to a neutral bias on interest rates, with the risk being the RBNZ moves to an easing bias because New Zealand inflation is very low despite a well-performing domestic economy, said Richard Grace head of currency strategy at CBA. Falling dairy prices and a contractionary budget will also weigh on growth, he said. The New Zealand rates market is likely to further price the risk of RBNZ rate cuts, he added. Current market pricing has 25 basis points of RBNZ rate cuts by September. Grace said the rates market is likely to bring forward that pricing. (james.glynn@wsj.com; Twitter @JamesGlynnWSJ) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0604 GMT [Dow Jones] ANZ Bank says it sees scope for further corrective gains in MYR, likely to be spurred by real money demand, as oil prices have finally rebounded. The bank thinks buying the Malaysian ringgit against the Thai baht is attractive. "While MYR will benefit from the bounce in oil prices, we see THB underperforming, given the subdued economic outlook. In addition, there is a possibility of rate cuts by the Bank of Thailand, which will weigh on THB," the bank says. ANZ Bank recommends buying MYR/THB via 3-month non-deliverable forward contracts at 9.1662 (spot reference 9.1807), targeting 9.6000 in spot with stop-loss at 9.0000. (jerry.tan@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0601 GMT [Dow Jones] Americans are feeling less stressed out in general than they were even before the recession, but money is the top source of emotional strain, with 72% of respondents feeling anxious about their finances at least some of the time over a single month, according to the annual Stress in America survey from the American Psychological Association. And financial stress appears to be bifurcating along income lines. While individuals in low-income and higher-income households reported the same level of strain in 2007, in 2014, a clear gap emerged, with those in families earning less than $50k reporting a 5.2 stress score on a scale of 10, where 10 is extreme stress, versus 4.7 in families earning more. The organization found that overall stress levels dropped to 4.9 in 2014 from 6.2 in 2007. The poll of 3,068 adults was conducted in August.(lauren.weber@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0559 GMT [Dow Jones] The risk-sensitive New Zealand dollar is higher against the yen in mid-Asian trade Wednesday, last at 87.33 versus 86.49 late Tuesday, as gains in Tokyo stocks spurred more short-yen hedges, driving the Japanese currency lower against the Kiwi. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average was recently up 1.81% at 17,649. The Kiwi is also supported by comments from Reserve Bank of New Zealand Gov. Graeme Wheeler, which were deemed less dovish than markets had been expecting. Wheeler said "in our current situation there are important considerations why a period of [official cash rate] stability is the most prudent option." Further upside in NZD/JPY may encounter resistance at 87.86 (38.2% Fibonacci correction of 94.05-84.03 Dec. 29-Feb. 3 decline), then at 88.33 (Jan. 28 minor reaction high) and the 200-day moving average (now at 88.54). (jerry.tan@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0549 GMT [Dow Jones] The AUD may fall further even after unexpected monetary easing by the Reserve Bank of Australia yesterday, says Mizuho Bank chief market economist Daisuke Karakama in a note. The RBA statement signaled further AUD weakness is needed and further rate cuts are inevitable, says Mr. Karamaka. "There is no way other than to adjust the currency or wages of a country at the time of excessive cost increases at home. And Australia is now in the course of doing it." Mr. Karakama says the AUD/USD (now at 0.7821) and the AUD/JPY (92.09) may fall to 0.71 and 84, respectively, by the end of this year. These levels are based on the AUD purchasing power parity that overshoots its current value by 9%. But he says the AUD often stays below PPP in historic patterns, adding that the AUD seemed to have been overvalued since the natural resources boom in 2005.(hiroyuki.kachi@wsj.com)

The official statistics agency will release the GDP data Thursday around 0400 GMT. (i-made.sentana@wsj.com)

title: USD/Asia Slides as Greece Fears Recede, Oil Jumps -- Asia Daily  Forex  Outlook
text:
The following are projected trading ranges and outlooks for nine secondary currency pairs in Asia today: 


 
          Immediate Range  Larger Range

(Ranges are calculated using recent highs and lows, information on the placement of option strikes, and technical analysis--Bollinger Bands, Fibonacci levels, trendlines and moving averages.)

USD/CNY--uptrend may end. Spot USD/CNY could drop out of its Bollinger uptrend channel if the People's Bank of China adjusts the daily USD/CNY benchmark rate lower in line with the U.S. dollar index. Overnight, the greenback fell as the euro and the Australian dollar rebounded sharply on the possibility that the Greek negotiation with the Troika could take much longer than expected. Stocks also rallied, further dampening demand for the safe haven U.S. dollar. If spot USD/CNY ends Wednesday below 6.2460 the bullish chart signal will be extinguished and the pair might retreat further to the 20-day Bollinger mid support at 6.2237. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for spot USD/CNY is at 6.2460 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 6.2237 (20-day Bollinger mid support). Immediate resistance is at 6.2684 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 6.2719 (top of monthly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/TWD--possible downtrend. USD/TWD could adopt a bearish technical bias after the U.S. dollar sank overnight on a letup in anxiety over Greece. The USD/TWD pair may attempt to break down into the Bollinger downtrend channel at 31.320. A Wednesday close below this mark could trigger more USD short-selling toward the base of the daily Ichimoku Cloud support at 31.090. The price difference between the 1-month USD/TWD nondeliverable forward contract and the spot contract is likely to drop from a premium into a discount as the short-term dollar view flips. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 31.480 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 31.320 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 31.090 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support). Immediate resistance is likely at 31.580 (20-day Bollinger mid), then at 31.840 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 32.000 (round-figure trading barrier).

USD/KRW--consolidation lower. USD/KRW gaps lower Wednesday to open at 1,093.0 versus its last close of 1,097.4, reflecting the overnight plunge of the U.S. dollar index due to the euro and the Australian dollar rebounding significantly. The daily chart may turn bearish for USD/KRW on a Wednesday close below the daily Ichimoku Cloud support zone at 1,084. Overnight, pressure on the euro - stemming from Greece's renegotiation of its bailout terms - eased as Germany said that the process could take months to pan out. The resulting bounce in the euro, which depressed the U.S. dollar index, has filtered into Asia where the U.S. dollar has fallen sharply across the board. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 1,090 (round-figure trading barrier), then at 1,087 (20-day Bollinger mid support), before 1,084 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support). Immediate resistance is at 1,095 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 1,098 (top of daily Ichimoku Cloud), before 1,100 (round-figure trading barrier).

USD/SGD--uptrend nullified. USD/SGD has fallen out of the daily Bollinger uptrend channel as the dollar sank overnight against the euro and Australia dollar and risk appetite returned with U.S. stocks rising 1.4%. USD/SGD could make its way to the 20-day Bollinger mid support at 1.3398 next. The catalyst for the overnight change in market sentiment was ostensibly the delay of a resolution in the Greece debt renegotiation process. Additionally, oil prices bounced sharply higher on the possibility that Saudi Arabia might cut production if Russia were to withdraw its support for President Assad in Syria. Data released late Tuesday showed Singapore's manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 49.9 in January against 49.6 in December, but remained in the sub-50 contractionary realm. Dow Jones technical analysis shows immediate support is at 1.3400 (round-figure trading barrier), then at 1.3398 (20-day Bollinger mid support), before 1.3314 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 1.3481 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 1.3500 (round-figure trading barrier), before 1.3565 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/MYR--possible downtrend. USD/MYR reopens after a two-day market closure, and plunges to 3.5690 from its last close of 3.6290, implying a 1.7% appreciation of the ringgit versus the U.S. dollar. If USD/MYR ends the day below 3.5700 the daily Bollinger downtrend channel will be activated and could motivate short-selling of the U.S. dollar by short-term speculative traders. The catalyst for the steep ringgit move was a sharp rebound in crude oil prices over the last two days. Production cuts in other parts of the world prompted bottom-picking in oil prices, while Saudi Arabia entertaining the possibility of cutting oil production if Russia withdraws support in Syria gave a more significant boost. The ringgit is still oil-sensitive despite recent attempts by the Malaysia government to downplay its influence on the local economy. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 3.5500 (psychological support), then at 3.5440 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 3.5700 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 3.5950 (20-day Bollinger mid resistance), before 3.6000 (round-figure trading barrier).

USD/THB--consolidation. USD/THB could stabilize on speculation that the Bank of Thailand may be attempting to support the pair to prevent excessive baht strength. A trader said the BOT might be trying to cap the baht at 32.50, avoiding the triggering of stoploss orders past the 200-day moving average line at 32.45. This may be why USD/THB is not lower alongside other regional pairs which sank at Wednesday's open due to overnight U.S. dollar weakness. A resurgence of the euro overnight - on the possibility that Greece renegotiation of its debt obligations could take months - depressed the U.S. dollar index and triggered a reaction in most parts of Asia Wednesday. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 32.55 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 32.45 (200-day moving average), before 32.43 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 32.66 (daily Ichimoku Cloud resistance and 20-day Bollinger mid resistance), before 32.78 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/PHP--downtrend. USD/PHP is likely to sink past the 44.00 round-figure trading barrier due to a sharp drop in the U.S. dollar index overnight coupled with a resurgence of risk-taking in stocks. The possible delay of a Greek default on its debt obligations has given the euro a reprieve and prompted capitulation of safe haven risk-off positions. An overnight rebound of the Australian dollar - reversing its the post-RBA rate cut drop - also disrupted bullish-USD sentiment. Besides the current negative fundamentals for the U.S. dollar index, two important USD/PHP chart resistance levels continue to prove resilient, encouraging more bearish bets in USD/PHP. The ceiling of the daily Bollinger downtrend channel at 44.14 as well as the 200-day moving average line at 44.25 managed to fend off bouts of U.S. dollar strength this week. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 44.00 (round-figure trading barrier and base of weekly Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 43.77 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 43.50 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is likely at 44.14 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 44.25 (200-day moving average), before 44.50 (psychological resistance).

USD/IDR--consolidation lower. USD/IDR could fall back into the daily Ichimoku Cloud support zone as the U.S. dollar index slumped overnight due to a sharp bounce of the euro. If USD/IDR ends the day below 12,500 and inside the daily Bollinger downtrend channel, there could be a chance of a further downward move to the Cloud support base at 12,440. The greenback slumped overnight as the euro surged on the likelihood that a Greek renegotiation with the Troika could be protracted, and on analysis that the country has sufficient reserves to pay off its existing debt obligations for several months. U.S. stocks rallied 1.4% as investors trimmed risk-off positions, adding to the positive market sentiment and thus helping emerging market assets. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for spot USD/IDR is at 12,580 (20-day Bollinger mid support and daily Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 12,500 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 12,440 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support). Immediate resistance is at 12,660 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 12,740 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 12,800 (psychological resistance).

A Wednesday close below 61.45 would engage the bearish technical channel that might lead to more rupee strength versus the U.S. dollar in the near term. title: India Imported Crude Oil Prices Rise -- Market Talk
text:
0736 GMT [Dow Jones] India's oil ministry said the price of its imported crude-oil basket rose to $45.33 a barrel Thursday from $43.36 Thursday, reflecting volatility in global crude prices. Oil futures took a breather from a selloff in Asian trade Friday as investors looked for signs of tighter supply that could stem further declines in oil prices. On Thursday, OPEC lowered its forecast for oil supply growth from non-OPEC members, but it also cut its forecast for world oil demand growth in 2015 by 70,000 barrels a day from its last report. A fall in oil prices is positive for India as it imports three-quarters of its energy needs. (saurabh.chaturvedi@wsj.com; Twitter: @journosaurabh) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0734 GMT [Dow Jones] It is doubtful the Swiss National Bank, in suddenly letting its currency rise against the euro, wanted to cause so much pain. But it likely did so knowing the ECB was poised to launch a new bond-buying program in the hopes of stimulating the region's struggling economy. That move would probably weaken the euro against other currencies because the bank would effectively be printing euros to buy bonds. But since the Swiss had committed to not allowing the franc to strengthen, the bank would have to sell francs and buy euros. The result would be the central bank ends up holding billions of dollars in the very currency its trying to fight against, in this case, the euro. For the Swiss central bank, that would mean 43% of its foreign currency investments were in euros, leaving it with a huge exposure to a decline in the euro. (ken.brown@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: KLH 

0723 GMT [Dow Jones]--The Swiss National Bank's scapping of its cap for the franc-euro will hurt exports and the economy, but is unlikely to push the country into recession, according to Credit Suisse. "If the euro-franc settles at current levels, Swiss export growth could come to a standstill this year, implying that GDP growth could be 0.5% to a maximum of 1%," says economist Maxime Botteron. The bank had previously forecast 2015 growth of 1.6%. "However, given still good momentum in the domestic economy the risk of a recession in Switzerland looks very low to us," he argues. EUR/CHF was last at 1.0198. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com) 


 
Contact us in London. +44-20-7842-9464 
markettalk@wsj.com 
 

0712 GMT [Dow Jones] NTPC (532555.BY), India's largest power generation utility, has signed for a 100 billion rupee loan agreement with the State Bank of India (500112.BY). The loan, which has a tenure of 15 years, will be utilized to part finance the company's capital expenditure programme, the power company said in a statement. NTPC has a total electricity generation capacity of 43.12 gigawatts and plans to have a generation capacity of 128 gigawatts by 2032. NTPC shares are trading 0.57% higher at 140.05 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange, while the benchmark index is almost flat. (saurabh.chaturvedi@wsj.com; Twitter: @journosaurabh) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0707 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/JPY will likely be well-supported around 115 for some time, with dip-buying at that level as long as expectations for the U.S. economy remain unchanged, says Minori Uchida, chief market analyst at global markets research at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi UFJ. But if expectations for eventual rate increases recede in the wake of upcoming U.S. economic indicators for January, the dollar may fall below 115 toward 114 or 113. Uchida says the USD at around Y110 would be consistent with the gap between U.S. and Japanese bond yields. Expectations for the U.S. economy and the likelihood of ECB easing inflate the USD at prevailing rates. While the former have been tempering, an actual ECB decision as early as next week may translate into slight USD selling after the market digests the headlines. (hiroyuki.kachi@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0705 GMT (Dow Jones) Scheduled government bond issuance in the eurozone is set to slow somewhat next week after two very busy weeks. Hence, Spain is one of the most likely candidates to use the current benign primary [government bond] market environment with a new syndicated 10-year deal, say Commerzbank strategists. A further factor in favor of the possible timing is that the 10-year maturity wouldn't face any scheduled peer pressure next week. (emese.bartha@wsj.com; @EmeseBartha) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0703 GMT [Dow Jones] Banks are still coming to terms with the trading losses arising from the Swiss National Bank's abrupt decision to scrap the cap on the Swiss franc Thursday. Some banks have apparently resorted to cancelling deals that clients executed on the electronic trading platforms--at the risk of losing these customers. The platforms weren't fast enough to widen their spreads--the gap between the buy and sell rates for EUR/CHF--because such an adjustment typically requires human input. Market chatter is that a second-tier bank has chalked up losses of around $50 million just on trades executed over the e-commerce platform. A top-tier bank would arguably have lost significantly more. One trader said some of these banks have negotiated with customers to adjust the rate at which their stoploss orders were 'filled'--in favor of the bank. Clients' orders to sell EUR/CHF in the event of a break of the 1.2000 floor would have been impossible to execute at a fair rate due to the sudden loss of bids in the market when the SNB stepped away from 3 years of artificially propping it up. (ewen.chew@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0703 GMT [Dow Jones] Once U.S. crude prices fall below $40/barrel or thereabouts, oil production will start shutting down in North America and the North Sea, James Hubbard, head of Asian oil research at Macquarie Group says. "Below $40 you can look for about 1.5 million barrels a day of supply to be cash flow negative," he says. He says eventually some of the current oversupply will start to disappear pretty quickly. "We might not be at the bottom now at around $45. [Prices] could go down another $10 ... but we're close," he says. February Nymex crude is up $0.32 at $46.57/barrel, March Brent crude rose $0.32 to $48.59/barrel. (eric.yep@wsj.com) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0646 GMT [Dow Jones] The NZD/USD is trading slightly higher as market focus remains on the unexpected decision by the Swiss National Bank to remove the cap on the EUR/CHF, says Western Union Business Solutions Corporate Dealing Manager Chris Hunter. "It has allowed the Kiwi to jump and hold gains other majors simply because they're obviously on the back foot against the Swiss franc." The pair is at 0.7833 vs. 0.7817 early this morning. Hunter puts support for the pair at 0.7790 with resistance coming in at 0.7890. Hunter says markets will now look to U.S. inflation to see if it can offset weakness in the USD/CHF. (lucy.craymer@wsj.com;Twitter: @lucy_craymer) 


 
Editor: AAP 
 

0615 GMT [Dow Jones] UBS lowers its forecasts for Swiss gross domestic product growth this year and next as the central bank's decision to scrap its cap for the franc-euro will drag on exports and the economy. UBS now sees growth in 2015 at just 0.5%, compared with its previous forecast of 1.8%. For 2016, it now expects growth of 1.1%, down from a previous forecast of 1.7%. "Industry wise, watch exporters are likely to be most negatively affected given a high share of franc-based costs," says Chief Investment Officer Mark Haefele. "Banks also have a high share of franc costs, while client assets are predominantly denominated in euros and dollars," he notes. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com) 


 
Editor: TFD 
 

0545 GMT [Dow Jones] Japanese retail currency investors, known collectively as "Mrs. Watanabe," appear to be suffering losses after unprecedented swings in the CHF, following a surprise move by Switzerland's central bank Thursday to scrap its policy of capping the CHF against the EUR. Industry sources say that Japan's financial authorities are conducting hearings into how much individual investors have lost, including their initial margin deposits and amounts paid by foreign exchange margin trading firms on behalf of their customers. An FX margin trading firm manager says the amount of losses individual investors might not be so huge since USD/JPY trading dominates about 80% of their trading. The manager estimates losses for retail investors stemming from the CHF movements could be as much as Y1 billion in total. "The move was historically unprecedented in terms of the degree of change within an hour," the manager says. The EUR/CHF plunged about 30% within a hour. Price volatility was exaggerated when all interbank traders stopped displaying bids-and-offers for a period. (tatsuo.ito@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: PJK 
 

0539 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/INR is lower than its Thursday close of 62.06, implying a stronger rupee versus the U.S. dollar, but speculation that the central bank is keeping it from gaining too fast may be holding USD/INR back for now. The Reserve Bank of India was suspected of intervening on Thursday--after cutting its repo rate to make it cheaper for banks to borrow money--to quell the rupee's 1.0% gain, says an offshore trader. The RBI could still be lurking around, supporting the bids in USD/INR around its current level of 61.92. If, however, the central bank steps away and USD/INR closes Friday below the 61.68 floor of the daily Ichimoku Cloud support zone, a bearish-dollar technical signal will be activated. Chart-motivated traders could then be encouraged to short the dollar versus the rupee for a near-term target of 61.00. (ewen.chew@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: MNG

0540 GMT [Dow Jones] Insurers are sharply lower after the yield on the benchmark 10-year Japanese Government Bond (JGB) dropped to 0.235% on Friday--a fresh record low. Rates for 20-year JGBs hit 0.895%, while the 30s hit 1.08%--both the lowest since the Bank of Japan introduced quantitative and qualitative easing in April 2013. Dai-Ichi Life (8750.TO) is down 4.1% at Y1,547, and T&D Holdings (8795.TO) is off 2.3% at Y1,282. "Cheap crude prices will keep inflation down and kill profits for life insurers, which typically have huge stocks of JGBs in their investment portfolios," says Norihiro Fujito, senior investment strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities. "Oil is the main inflation driver globally. But it may take months to years before the crude market turns around." Yields on 5-year JGBs remain at 0.0%, which they hit for the first time Tuesday.(bradford.frischkorn@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0536 GMT [Dow Jones] Record-high electricity consumption in December in China was likely the effect of seasonal factors--heating at the onset of winter and factories restarting after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in November--rather than an outright demand recovery, analysts say. China said Friday it consumed a record 511.7 billion kilowatt-hours in December, up 4.7% from a year earlier. "The question is the growth--it's the most important indicator and it's in line with figures that show the economy is still slowing," said investment bank North Square Blue Oak's Miao Tian. The pace of growth just matches levels in the first half of this year, when growth was still relatively anemic. (chuin-wei.yap@wsj.com; Twitter @YapCW) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0529 GMT [Dow Jones] Thailand's central bank is less worried about high household debt in 2015 after its growth has appeared to be slowing down in recent months. "The household debt problem is not worrying because consumption-related loans [now] account for 3 in 10 of total loans," says Tongurai Limpiti, a deputy governor at the Bank of Thailand. "Outstanding consumer loans currently stand at 3.44 trillion baht [$105 billion], compared with outstanding loans of 11.08 trillion baht [$339 billion]." The central reported earlier that Thailand's household debt was 83.5% of gross domestic product in the second quarter of 2014. Tongurai also notes that the Bank of Thailand does not expect non-performing loans to rise considerably in the first quarter of this year after its ratio was at 2.34% in third quarter 2014, compared with 2.15% for 2014. (nopparat.chaichalearmmongkol@dowjones.com) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0510 GMT [Dow Jones] Oil markets are feeling some of the impact after the Swiss National Bank removed its currency cap against the euro, analyst Daniel Ang at Singapore's Phillip Futures says. He says the U.S. dollar index has soared and the euro weakened, weighing on oil prices. "We previously identified the bottom for crude prices to be at $46 for Brent and $43 for west Texas intermediate. Prices are indeed showing heavy support here suggesting that we could be the bottom already," he adds. "All our forecasts seem to point towards a consolidation stage in the weeks to come," Ang says, adding that crude prices may stay rangebound. February Nymex crude is up $0.32 at $46.57 a barrel, March Brent crude rose $0.32 to $48.59 a barrel. (eric.yep@wsj.com) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0500 GMT [Dow Jones] Kaisa Group's (1638.HK) problems with blocked apartments, which appeared to have spread to a second Chinese city, underscore a feature of the Chinese property market: Many developers sell apartments before they are completed. That gives developers needed cash to complete projects. But accounts of angry Kaisa homeowners seeking answers to the fate of their apartments could give future buyers at other projects pause. This also highlights the urgency for property developers to seek alternative funding for the construction of homes. A real-estate portal in Hangzhou says more than 700 apartments at a Kaisa development there have been frozen. It already faces blocked apartments in Shenzhen. (esther.fung@wsj.com; Twitter: @estherfung) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0419 GMT [Dow Jones] Chinese stocks were higher at the lunchtime break, with the Shanghai Composite last up 1% at 3371.23, as the index was on track for its tenth consecutive weekly gain--its longest winning streak since 2007. The market remained buoyant following Thursday's lending data. Loan growth is slowing in China but total social financing--which encompasses shadow banking credit--picked up. The total social financing number from yesterday "is certainly helping," says David Welch, head of equity sales trading at Reorient Group. "But the number speaks to a broader issue in that China has room for more monetary easing," he said. The Shenzhen Composite adds 0.9% to 1473.42. (Daniel.Inman@wsj.com) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0415 GMT [Dow Jones] Indian shares opened lower Friday, tracking weak cues from regional markets and also due to profit-booking after Thursday's sharp rise. The S&P BSE Sensex was down 0.4% at 27977.64, while the National Stock Exchange's Nifty index fell 0.4% to 8463.60. The benchmark Sensex index jumped 2.7% on Thursday following a surprise rate cut by the Reserve Bank of India. Analysts said investors will now watch the government's moves to speed up reforms. Tata Consultancy Services (532540.BY) declined 1.7% after it posted only a 5% increase in its fiscal third-quarter profit. Other Sensex losers include Bharti Airtel (532454.BY), Tata Steel (500470.BY), ICICI Bank (532174.BY) and State Bank of India (500112.BY). (debiprasad.nayak@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: FLS 
 

0411 GMT [Dow Jones] Louis Cooper, Managing Director of OANDA, an online retail currency trading house, says the unexpected decision by SNB will continue to produce fallout in the markets over coming weeks as the "speed and ferocity" of the market movements have exposed undercapitalized participants. Cooper said OANDA itself experienced "significant losses" but is managing the "historic" situation". "We are a very well capitalized business. There are players that won't be." The shock to markets ranks among the biggest seen in recent years, and it has been amplified by the fact that the SNB had given no indication of change, and indeed, had affirmed its commitment to the cap only recently, Cooper added. "Some of these providers will not be able to maintain business as usual and even worse will be going out of business. I think this is the start of more news coming over the next few days," Cooper said. (james.glynn@wsj.com; Twitter @JamesGlynnWSJ) 


 
Editor: KLH 
 

0346 GMT [Dow Jones] The Swiss National Bank's surprise move to decouple the franc from the euro has been one of the strongest hints to date that the European Central Bank is ready to actively weaken the euro and embark on a bond-buying program at its January 22 meeting, says Ben Alexander, who is overseeing a fixed-interest portfolio of A$5.6 billion at Ardea Investment Management in Sydney. "Europe is a mess", he says, predicting that Australian government debt will now become even more attractive to offshore buyers. A fresh proof of the strong demand came overnight, when the benchmark 10-year bond yield dropped to a new record low of 2.509%. (vera.sprothen@wsj.com) 


 
Editor: JFN 
 

0338 GMT [Dow Jones] Vietnam's Finance Ministry said the Japan Bank for International Cooperation is offering to help the Vietnamese government raise funds selling yen-denominated bonds in Japan. The ministry said in a statement JBIC has introduced some Japanese advisers for the bond sales, including SMBC Nikko. No details on any planned bond sales are available. The ministry added that it is also encouraging Japanese investors to buy Vietnam's government dong-denominated bonds. (trong-khanh.vu@wsj.com; Twitter: @TrongKhanhVu) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0336 GMT [Dow Jones] The Swiss National Bank's policy volte-face on Thursday briefly interrupted a meeting of Allianz's chief investment officers, who immediately began discussing how to take advantage of the Swiss franc's move, says Andreas Utermann, global chief investment officer at AllianzGlobal Investors. He told colleagues he should short the franc to make a quick profit from the central bank's action. "But by the time we got our heads around it, it had already recovered... so we said let's get on with our meeting," he said. "It took about 15 minutes, and that was an opportunity lost, but so what." Still, he said he profited from the Swiss franc's appreciation: "Unless you were short the Swiss franc against the euro, which probably very few people were, how would you lose money yesterday?" (gregor.hunter@wsj.com; Twitter @gregorhunter)

The overnight fall of copper prices has taken over the spotlight from crude oil's recent collapse; markets are blaming China - the world's biggest consumer of the base metal - as part of the reason for the drop in prices. The slowdown in demand from China is a reminder that the government is shifting away from manufacturing-led economic growth and attempting to build a more consumption-centric economy. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for spot USD/CNY is at 6.1895 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 6.1800 (psychological support), before 6.1658 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support zone). Immediate resistance is at 6.1995 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 6.2000 (round-figure trading barrier), before 6.2096 (20-day Bollinger mid resistance).

USD/TWD could take on a bearish chart bias if it closes Thursday below the 31.600 entrance to the daily Bollinger downtrend channel. The price difference between the benchmark 1-month USD/TWD contract and that of the spot contract may fall back under par - from its current premium of 0.015 - as U.S. dollar weakness spreads. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 31.760 (20-day Bollinger mid support), then at 31.600 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 31.500 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is likely at 31.920 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 32.000 (round-figure trading barrier), before 32.080 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

The BOK monetary policy decision due at 0100 GMT could weaken the won if a dovish stance is adopted. Since late last year, analysts have been suggesting that the BOK could cut rates to stimulate growth - an argument more pertinent now that the World Bank has lowered global growth expectations for 2015. USD/KRW is however still in the daily Bollinger downtrend channel that caps at 1,088. A Thursday close above this barrier would negate the bearish technical bias and open the way to the 20-day Bollinger mid resistance line at 1,096. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 1,080 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support and round-figure trading barrier), then at 1,070 (round-figure trading barrier), before 1,068 (weekly Ichimoku Cloud support). Immediate resistance is at 1,088 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 1,090 (round-figure trading barrier), before 1,096 (20-day Bollinger mid resistance).

USD/SGD--consolidation. USD/SGD has been flitting in and out of the daily Bollinger uptrend channel but may consolidate lower as the continued drop in U.S government bond yields makes it less attractive to hold the U.S. dollar. The overnight fall of USD/JPY - a lead indicator for the region - is also a factor that may prevent USD/SGD from entering the Bollinger uptrend channel. The yield on the benchmark U.S. 10-year government bond has fallen to around 1.84% after weaker-than-expected U.S. retail sales data. Sustained demand for safe-haven bonds has been depressing the yield on U.S. Treasurys. Dow Jones technical analysis shows immediate support is at 1.3300 (round-figure trading barrier), then at 1.3280 (20-day Bollinger mid support), before 1.3214 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 1.3358 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 1.3400 (round-figure trading barrier), before 1.3412 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

But the daily Bollinger uptrend channel remains in effect - contingent on a Thursday close above 3.5670 - which could keep USD/MYR buoyant. Oil prices got a reprieve as focus shifted to copper - which fell substantially on Wednesday. But bearish forecasts for oil by global investment banks as well as oil producer Saudi Arabia are unlikely to be brushed off in the near term. The persistent weakness of oil prices has been hurting investor sentiment for the ringgit because Malaysia's trade balance - as an oil producer and exporter - will be adversely affected. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 3.5670 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 3.5280 (20-day Bollinger mid support). Immediate resistance is at 3.6000 (round-figure trading barrier), then at 3.6070 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 3.6200 (psychological resistance).

The pair entered the Bollinger downtrend channel on Tuesday but is also caught inside the daily Ichimoku Cloud support zone that spans 32.64-32.91. A break of the Cloud's base at 32.64 is necessary to trigger more U.S. dollar downside. The yield on the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury note fell further overnight to hit a 1.5-year low of 1.80%, due to demand for bonds from haven-seeking investors after weak U.S. retail sales data, hence depressing the greenback in general. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 32.75 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 32.64 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud support), before 32.50 (psychological support). The street expects little change in tone from the Indonesia central bank - especially since inflation is less of a threat given low commodity prices - but if BI sounds a cautious tone about growth prospects, the rupiah could react positively on expectations for easier monetary policy to come. title: India Starts Rolling out National Broadband Network -- Market Talk
text:
0439 GMT [Dow Jones] The Indian government has started rolling out a national broadband network from the southern state of Kerala. The network is aimed at taking government and individual services directly to citizens with the help of broadband. The network will also be used by telecom companies for providing internet services, and television cable companies. Through this network, India aims to cut transaction and traveling costs of citizens, which would boost economic growth. (krishna.jai@wsj.com; Twitter: @jaikrishna)

title: India Imported Crude Oil Price Falls Again -- Market Talk
text:
0712 GMT [Dow Jones] India's oil ministry said the price of its imported crude-oil basket fell to $45.86 a barrel Monday from $47.36 Friday, reflecting volatility in global crude prices. Oil prices fell for the second consecutive day with both the crude benchmarks down nearly 2% in Asian trade Tuesday. Oil prices had lost around 5% on Monday alone, extending the selloff that has gripped oil markets since mid-2014, as sell-side analysts slashed price forecasts and warned of a prolonged glut in global oil markets that will extend well into 2015. Markets have been fumbling around for a price floor, especially after the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries decided not to cut output to stem the decline in prices. A fall in crude-oil prices is positive for India's economy as the country imports three-quarters of its energy needs. (saurabh.chaturvedi@wsj.com; Twitter: @journosaurabh) 


 
Editor JSM 
 

0700 GMT [Dow Jones] Oil prices sunk Tuesday with the U.S. oil benchmark dropping below $45 a barrel after United Arab Emirates' oil minister said the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries won't adjust output, and that other producers need to be rational. He says oil prices could take two or three years to stabilize and OPEC is concerned about the oil-market balance, but that it can't be the only party responsible for balancing the market. The UAE is one of the 10 largest oil and natural gas producers in the world, and a member of OPEC. Nymex west Texas intermediate crude is down $1.08 at $44.99/barrel, Brent crude is down $1.28 at $46.15/barrel. (eric.yep@wsj.com)

0618 GMT [Dow Jones] The latest rebound in India's industrial output was primarily due to distortions caused by the change in timing of the Diwali festival this year, says HSBC. Adjusted for those effects, an industrial recovery still appears feeble, which, coupled with a better-than-expected inflation print, reinforces the case for rate cuts by the central bank. "Looking past these statistical quirks shows that the growth momentum in manufacturing is still weak," HSBC says. "We expect 50 basis points in rate cuts in 2015," it adds. India's industrial output rose 3.8% from a year earlier in November, after a 4.2% contraction the previous month. Meanwhile, the consumer inflation rate climbed to 5% in December from 4.38% in November, but was still better than the 5.40% prediction of economists. (anant.kala@wsj.com; @anantvkala)

title: UPDATE 3-Indian markets off lows, foreign investors in focus
text:
* Rupee ends at 63.615/625 per dlr, off 13-mth low

* NSE trims losses, ends down 0.5 pct

* 10-yr bond yield ends down 2 bps at 7.97 pct (Updates closing levels for rupee, debt)

By Swati Bhat

MUMBAI, Dec 17 (Reuters) - The rupee retreated from 13-month lows after the central bank stepped up intervention, while bonds also recovered despite concerns over whether foreign funds will stick with India, one of the star performers this year among emerging markets.

Intervention from the Reserve Bank of India was larger than in recent sessions, traders said, with some estimating dollar sales of nearly $500 million. Meanwhile, buying of shares by state-run Life Insurance Corporation of India helped shares recover from earlier falls to trade flat, dealers added.

Analysts fear more foreign selling, but doubt it would spark turmoil anywhere similar to last year when India suffered its worst market crisis since 1991.

Unlike then, India is now seen as benefitting from sharp falls in inflation, hefty foreign exchange reserves, and a less troublesome current account gap.

"We are less worried as overall market conditions are better, like fiscal condition is within control, current account deficit is low, inflation is falling," a senior policymaker aware of the central bank's thinking told Reuters, declining to be identified discussing the country's exchange rate policy.

The partially convertible rupee ended at 63.6150/6250 per dollar, weaker than its 63.53/54 close. It had earlier weakened to as much as 63.89, its lowest since Nov. 13, 2013.

The rupee's initial weakness came after foreign funds sold shares worth $196.56 million on Tuesday, their biggest daily net sales since Oct. 17, and a sixth consecutive day of selling.

Foreign investors also turned sellers of debt for the first time in December on Monday, having sold a net $146.56 million.

But analysts say India is better placed to withstand foreign selling, given the current account deficit has narrowed to 2.1 percent of gross domestic product from a record high of 4.8 percent in the fiscal year ended in March 2013.

Meanwhile, foreign currency reserves stood at $314.66 billion as of Friday, not far from the record high of $320.785 billion in September 2011.

India has attracted a combined $43.2 billion in foreign flows into debt and shares so far this year. As a result, the NSE index is still up around 25 percent in 2014, the second-best performer in Asia in dollar terms.

The benchmark 10-year bond yield hit a session high of 8.03 percent, its highest since Dec. 1, before retreating to end the day down 2 basis points at 7.97 percent. The yield is still up 14 bps for the week. (Editing by Rafael Nam, Sunil Nair and Jacqueline Wong)

title: Emerging-Market Selloff Rattles Asian Shares -- 4th Update
text:
A global emerging-market selloff rattled Asia for a second day Tuesday, sending stocks tumbling and forcing central banks in the region to intervene to slow declines in their currencies.

The selling started in Asia right away on Monday and reverberated around the world before pressuring the region further on Tuesday. India's rupee is at its weakest level in more than a year, while stocks in Singapore and Malaysia are off more than 2%.

Investors in Hong Kong sold as well, as China showed fresh slowing signs, while a surge in the safe-haven yen sent Japanese stocks down 2%.

Global investors are rushing out of riskier markets in Asia as the U.S. draws nearer to increasing interest rates, while a worsening slide in oil is also adding volatility to markets. The U.S. Federal Reserve will deliver its latest outlook Wednesday, which could send the dollar higher if it hints that it is moving closer to raising borrowing costs as the economy improves.

Currency declines have deepened as the contagion has broadened. Indonesia's central bank on Tuesday said it had bought government bonds and had intervened in the foreign-exchange market to stabilize the rupiah after it touched a fresh 16-year low Tuesday. Traders estimated the Indonesian central bank likely sold about $500 million Tuesday, higher than the approximately $250 million it sold on average since last week.

Traders also said they suspected that the Reserve Bank of Indiaintervened through the day Tuesday to abate the rupee's fall. The central bank wasn't immediately available for comment.

The selloff hit Asian bond markets as well. In India, yields ticked up as much as 0.13% Tuesday after recently falling to their lowest level in a year. In Indonesia, yields on 10-year benchmark government bonds jumped 0.20%, despite the central bank's move to buy government bonds. Yields move inversely to prices.

The two-day rout has been a break from a period of relative resilience in Asia, compared with emerging markets elsewhere. Stocks in India and much of Southeast Asia, for example, have run up double-digit percentage gains since the beginning of the year, and investors have favored Asian bonds and currencies for much of the year.

Lower oil prices are expected to help the parts of Asia that are net commodity importers, which could stem some of the selling. Stock losses in Thailand were milder Tuesday, after the benchmark SET plunged more than 9% during yesterday's trade. The market was last off 1.2% at 1461.15.

Binay Chandgothia, a portfolio manager at Principal Global Investors, which has $326 billion in assets under management, said he recently added exposure to emerging markets in Asia. The Fed meeting could produce further bouts of volatility, but Asia-Pacific selloffs this week are an opportunity to buy, he said.

China's market was more insulated, although fresh signs of a weaker domestic economy knocked Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index down 1.6% to close at 22670.50. HSBC's preliminary reading for China's Purchasing Managers Index for December came in at 49.5, signaling a contraction, compared with last month's 50. Economists expected the indicator to stay put at a six-month low.

The Shanghai Composite Index rose 2.3% to 3021.52, the highest since April 2011, on hopes that a weaker domestic economy would mean further policy easing and fiscal stimulus from Beijing.

The rupiah slid as much as 1.8% on Tuesday, hitting 12,930 against the U.S. dollar. It was last down 0.4% at 12,645. Meanwhile, the rupee was at its weakest point in more than a year against the U.S. dollar, after trade data Monday showed the country's deficit at its widest in 18 months. The rupee last traded at 63.4 against the U.S. dollar. The Indian rupee fell as much as 0.6% on Tuesday.

title: India's Inflation May Ease to New Lows in November -- Market Talk

title: Indian rupee recoups losses to end nearly flat
text:
* Rupee ends at 61.94/95 per dlr vs 61.96/97 on Wednesday

* Exporter dlr sales to resume if INR at 62.20/$1:FX strategist

* Traders spot likely dlr sales from RBI via state-owned banks

By Neha Dasgupta

MUMBAI, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The Indian rupee ended nearly flat on Thursday after a fall to a nine-month low had sparked mild intervention from the central bank, as emerging market currencies were hit by a weak reading in a private survey of China's manufacturing.

The China flash HSBC/Markit manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) fell to a six-month low in November, with output contracting for the first time in six months.

The falls in the rupee are raising the prospect of higher imported inflation, although the slump in global crude prices is tempering some of those concerns.

Analysts also note the rupee could prove sturdier than other emerging market economies given confidence about a recovery in the country's economy.

Earlier in the day, traders said the central bank was likely selling dollars through state-owned banks to stem the rupee's fall.

"We might see some retracement towards 61.90 (per dollar) and then some bounce again," said Hemal Doshi, a currency strategist at Geojit Comtrade Ltd.

"Exporters in India got 62 plus levels after a long time so they also sold today, and these dollar sales will keep coming around 62.20 levels," Doshi said.

The partially convertible rupee closed at 61.94/95 per dollar versus its previous close of 61.96/97, after earlier touching a low of 62.22, its weakest level since Feb. 20.

Besides falling emerging market currencies, the rupee was also pressured by state-owned banks spotted buying dollars as India is soon due to pay a third tranche of $400 million to Iran, allowing Tehran to recover part of its overseas frozen oil revenues.

The falls in the rupee spurred state-run banks to sell dollars on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India in spot markets, and heavier interventions in forward markets, according to traders.

In the offshore non-deliverable forwards, the one-month contract was at 62.26/36, while the three-month was at 62.83/93.

title: Indian rupee hits over 5-wk high; cbank steps in to check gains
text:
* Rupee ends at 60.29/30 per dollar vs 60.39/40 on Friday

* Cbank spotted buying dlrs to prevent further gains in rupee

* INR seen in range of 59.85 to 60.70 this week - trader

By Swati Bhat

MUMBAI, Sept 8 (Reuters) - The Indian rupee gained on Monday, hitting a more than five-week high, as the weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs data raised hopes about additional foreign inflows, although broader gains were capped after the central bank was spotted intervening.

The dollar slipped after data showed U.S. employers added the fewest jobs in eight months in August, eroding confidence in the economy and reviving bets that the Federal Reserve might leave interest rates near zero for longer than anticipated.

The Fed's easy monetary stance has sparked big foreign inflows into emerging markets, including India, where overseas funds have bought a net $31.9 billion worth of debt and shares so far this year.

Analysts said the focus will be now on domestic factors such as the consumer inflation data due on Friday as well as the central bank policy review at the end of the month. Still, few expected a significant appreciation in the rupee given the prospect of continued intervention from the Reserve Bank of India.

"Globally most major events are done. We will have to watch top state-run banks' action as it seems they are determined to prevent sharp appreciation in the rupee," said Hari Chandramgethen, head of foreign exchange trading at South Indian Bank.

The partially convertible rupee closed stronger at 60.29/30 versus Friday's close of 60.39/40.

Chandramgethen expects the rupee to hold in a range of 59.85 to 60.70 for the rest of the week.

Hopes of continued foreign flows helped the rupee climb to 60.20 in early trade, its highest level since July 30.

But the central bank sold dollars via state-run banks in both the spot and the forward markets to prevent further gains in the rupee, five traders said.

In the offshore non-deliverable forwards, the one-month contract was at 60.58 while the three-month was at 61.18.

title: India  Central Bank  Seen Holding Rupee Down to Protect Exports, Economy
text:
Investors pouring billions of dollars into India's rallying stock and bond markets are encountering a surprise: a weak currency.

The rupee has slumped 3% since the business-friendly Bharatiya Janata Party took power in May, in sharp contrast to the nation's stocks, which have risen 9.6% to record highs and are up 25% for the year, ranking as Asia's best performers.

The unusual divergence is the result of central bank's intervention in foreign-exchange markets, investors and analysts say, which is meant to prevent gains in the rupee that would make exports more expensive, put pressure on India's fragile finances and potentially derail the country's economic recovery.

It's also a sharp reversal from last summer's emerging-market rout, when investors fled India. Now the central bank is struggling with the opposite problem--how to cope with outsize pools of cash flowing in.

"The weakness in the rupee doesn't reflect disappointment over the new government's performance. On the contrary, foreign investor flows into debt and equity markets have been strong," said Suvir Mukhi, senior portfolio manager at Income Partners Asset Management in Hong Kong, which has $1.3 billion under management.

"The weakness reflects the [Reserve Bank of India's] intervention," as the central bank buys U.S. dollars and sells rupees to build its war chest, he said.

Mr. Mukhi said his fund recently added positions in Indian local currency bonds.

India's foreign-exchange reserves have grown by $26 billion so far this year to a record $320 billion. Analysts from Morgan Stanley estimate the central bank has bought a $59.5 billion of dollars in the currency markets since last November.

In an interview with The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday, Reserve Bank of India Governor Raghuram Rajan didn't comment directly on whether the central bank was intervening in currency markets.

"We have $320 billion in reserves--we can weather a lot of stuff with that. But I don't see the reserves as being the first line of defense. The first line of defense is our macroeconomic picture," he said.

Mitul Kotecha, head of foreign-exchange strategy in Asia-Pacific at Barclays, says the normally positive correlation between the Indian stock market and currency over the past year has flipped in the past three months. He forecasts the rupee strengthening 1.6% to 59.5 per U.S. dollar in the next three months, from 60.45 on Wednesday.

"The move in the equity and bond markets is inconsistent with the currency," Mr. Kotecha said. "If it wasn't for the Reserve Bank of India buying dollars, we would see a stronger currency and the reason is very much that they are preventing it from strengthening. That's why you've seen a divergence in the performance of equities and bonds, and the currency."

The inflows this year have been particularly heavy, and the rupee's slump isn't deterring money managers who continue to turn to India. This month, investors have put $3.2 billion into the country's markets, bringing the total for the year so far to $29.6 billion, the most year-to-date in the past five years.

Ashley Perrot, head of pan-Asia fixed income at UBS Asset Management in Singapore, says the attraction is high yields. The yield on the benchmark 10-year bond is 8.5%, compared with 8.27% in Indonesia and 3.9% in Malaysia.

Still, India's economic woes are far from over. Inflation remains high, export growth is slowing and the trade deficit widened last month, though it is still narrower than at the height of the emerging-market turmoil last year.

"India has walked to its own drum," said Sacha Tihanyi, senior currency strategist at Scotiabank in Hong Kong. "I don't see a good reason for the rupee to be strengthening, economically speaking, too much on a sustained basis."

Mr. Tihanyi forecast the rupee to weaken 4% to 63 per U.S. dollar by the end of the year.

Most investors are hoping the new government can introduce structural reforms that will open up various sectors of the economy and take pressure off inflation. They say the rupee's decline has been orderly this time around and isn't a sign of renewed gloom toward the economy or policy.

"There is the hope that politicians will get it right and the market has given them the benefit of the doubt for the time being," Mr. Perrot said. He owns more 10-year government bonds than the benchmark he tracks recommends.

Gabriele Parussini contributed to this article.
