title: India confident in face of nuclear sanctions.
text:
BOMBAY, May 14 (Reuters) - India is confident its economy can weather U.S. sanctions imposed after its nuclear tests this week. 

 "There is absolutely nothing to indicate any loss of confidence among investors either in the stock market, or in the currency market, or in the economy," Finance Minister Yashwant Sinha told reporters late on Thursday. 

 India's greatest fear is not of the sanctions themselves, but fear they could precipitate a loss of faith in the country's economy. 

 Following India's nuclear tests the United States said more than $20 billion of aid, loans and trade will be put on ice through sanctions that take effect next month. 

 Japan, India's biggest donor, has order a block on around $1 billion of aid loans and a host of European countries have curtailed aid also. 

 Indian officials say the impact of the U.S. sanctions will be small, as much of the $20 billion is tied to future commitments. 

 And sanctions will hopefully have passed away long before these commitments are due for execution, as all sides scramble to find a diplomatic resolution to the furore. 

 An early Indian signature on the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty would go a long way to soothing the international community's anger with New Delhi. 

 But for now members of the Hindu revivalist Bhartiya Janata Party led coalition have begun a damage limitation exercise to dispel nagging doubts that sanctions could damage the country. 

 Commerce Minister Ramakrishna Hegde warned Washington's actions would hurt American firms doing business here more than India. 

 And Power Minister Rangarajan Kumaramangalam said India could manage without even multilateral financing for its power projects - the infrastructure sector the government has given the highest priority. 

 Meantime, the actual effects on near-term capital inflows will be manageable, officials say. 

 "The direct impact from the U.S. sanctions on capital flows will not be much," said a senior banking official. 

 Doubts on that score finally broke the lock on the rupee on Thursday after it had held steady at below 39.80 since the threat of sanctions first surfaced following Monday's first series of nuclear tests. 

 The rupee closed at 40.51/55, after touching an all time low of 40.77 earlier in the day. 

 Sinha said the rupee's recovery from lows showed the market mechanism was in place. 

 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) refrained from intervening on Thursday, judging conditions fast but not panicky given the extraordinary events. 

 Also the RBI says it has no level in mind for the rupee, and some analysts reckon the central bank is sanguine about letting the currency weaken so long as the moves are orderly and justified. 

 But the preservation of confidence appeared to be at play earlier this week when State Bank of India (SBI), which is often regarded as a surrogate for the central bank, sold dollars to keep the rupee steady after news broke of the nuclear tests. 

 There was also speculation that heavy buying of stocks by the country's largest mutual fund was a veiled attempt by the authorities to keep confidence levels from running too low in financial markets. 

 Thursday's close on the benchmark Bombay top 30 index was just three percent down from levels seen before the nuclear storm broke. 

 Fund managers say London's global depository receipt (GDR) market provides a purer gauge of sentiment toward India. 

 The HSBC India GDR index has come down 11 percent in the period, and the GDRs premium over local share prices has fallen to just over seven percent, after having traded at a 15-20 percent premium for the past month. 

 The authorities are monitoring the behaviour of foreign financial institutions (FIIs) in India for signs of trouble. 

 FIIs have invested around $9 billion in India since they first came to the country in 1993. Until last November they built up their investment a little more every month. 

 But in four of the last six months FIIs posted net outflows from India, and the negative trend continued in this month. 

 The scale of the outflow has been small - just $27 million of portfolio investment was pulled out in April, although $32 million left the country in the first week of May. 

 The authorities are not alarmed, and expect the FIIs to top up their investments when the dust has settled, and possibly reap the profits afforded foreigners by a cheaper rupee.

title: Indian rupee fall seen narrowing trade deficit.
text:
BOMBAY, Jan 31 (Reuter) - The Indian rupee's rapid slide against the dollar need not ring alarm bells as industry stands largely to benefit and a slowdown in imports could narrow the trade deficit, analysts said on Wednesday. 

 "It may narrow the deficit between imports and exports," said R. Balakrishnan, head of research at DSP Financial Consultants, the Indian associate of Merrill Lynch. 

 The trade gap for the year ending on March 31, 1996, is officially projected at $4.0 billion but many analysts had expected it to exceed this figure. 

 The rupee started falling in August 1995 after holding steady at 31.37 per dollar for almost two years. It fell to an all-time low of 36.63/70 on Wednesday despite sporadic intervention by the Reserve Bank of India, the central bank. 

 "I think this level is comfortable," said Balakrishnan. "Further fall will mean the rupee is undervalued." 

 Ashwini Agarwal, head of research at Indian investment firm SSKI Securities, said the fall looked bad. "But if you examine it, is is healthy for domestic industry." 

 Agarwal said the depreciation meant added protection for Indian manufacturers from imports. Balakrishnan said Indian firms producing commodity plastics and man-made fibres, like Reliance Industries, and Indian Petrochemicals Corporation, would benefit from the rupee's fall. 

 Agarwal said the fear of a slowdown in foreign investment was unwarranted as overseas investors had built in depreciation of the Indian currency in their calculations. 

 "In the long term, it will be beneficial," he said. 

 Analysts said the fall of the rupee was negative for the government as it would see external debt payments rise in rupee terms, driving the fiscal deficit higher. 

 Another negative for the economy is the fear that the weakening rupee will fuel inflation, which has been contained to single-digit levels for the last several months. 

 Annual inflation as measured by the wholesale price index stands at 5.08 percent against 11.89 percent a year ago. 

 India has not revised its government-fixed petroleum product prices for over a year. Petroleum products account for around one-fifth of the country's total import bill. 

 Many analysts believe the government has postponed revision of petroleum prices because of general elections expected in April and due by mid-1996. 

 Bank dealers said they would not rule out a further fall in the value of the rupee because of a near-panic. 

 "Potentially it could shoot out to 38 per dollar in the middle of the year if there is no majority government after April's parliament election, but by the year-end you can see it recovering," Chris Tinker, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank, told Reuters in London on Tuesday. 

 Leading Indian firms are covering their import payables in the forward market as they fear the rupee could fall further. 

 Exporters, expecting the rupee to fall further, are still not converting their dollars into rupees in the spot market. 

 "We were selling some dollars for August-delivery at 39.20 in the morning," said an executive of an Indian firm. "We have now raised it to 39.50," he said.

title: Indian rupee under pressure as importers panic.
text:
BOMBAY, Jan 8 (Reuter) - Panic buying of dollars by importers on Monday kept the Indian rupee under steady pressure despite an intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to arrest its fall, dealers said. 

 "Importers are panicking and buying dollars," said a dealer with a foreign bank. "It appears there is a general lack of confidence in the Indian currency." 

 Dealers said the RBI had intervened in the market as the rupee slipped to 35.54/57 per dollar in early trade from the opening 35.45/47. It fell further to 35.68 per dollar at midsession rendering RBI's intervention almost ineffective. 

 "The rupee is under pressure and will continue to be so unless something drastic is done," said another dealer. 

 Dealers said the RBI had been intervening on a daily basis and on Monday corporate demand for dollars appeared to have exceeded the central bank's dollar selling. 

 A spokesperson for the RBI confirmed the central bank's intervention but declined to give any figure. 

 Dealers said there had been speculation that some state-run firms, including the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation and the Indian Oil Coporation, were in the market for dollars. 

 Market analysts estimated the RBI intervention to be in the region of $40-50 million though some dealers put the figure as high as $90-100 million. 

 A Reuters poll in late December quoted foreign exchange analysts as saying that the rupee would slide by at least 5.6 percent against the dollar in 1996. 

 Meanwhile, bankers said the new overnight limits for banks set by the RBI would add depth to India's foreign exchange market amid renewed downward pressure on the rupee. 

 The RBI has scrapped a system limiting all banks to an outstanding overnight foreign exchange position equivalent to 150 million rupees and instead is authorising different levels for different banks based on their capital. 

 "Some major banks will get a large hike in the outstanding positions they are allowed," said one treasury manager. 

 Some bankers see the relaxation by the RBI adding to the volatility of the rupee, although others say the greater depth to the market could help iron out end-of-day fluctuations. 

 Demand for dollars in India is still mostly determined by export and import demand, with the rupee often fluctuating in line with major Indian oil purchases. Bankers say the market has a daily turnover of between $400 million and $1.0 billion. 

 While there is scope for speculation, bankers say the trend of the rupee is still driven by corporate demand.

title: India 's RBI will  intervene  as needed - governor.
text:
NEW DELHI, Dec 5 (Reuter) - Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor C. Rangarajan reiterated that the central bank will intervene when needed to make sure fluctuations in the value of the rupee are consistent with economic fundamentals. 

 "The Reserve Bank of India will continue to keep a close watch on developments in the foreign exchange market and intervene as necessary to make sure that market fluctuations are contained within reasonable limits and are consistent with the economic fundamentals," he said. 

 The central bank governor said the recent decline in the value of the rupee against the U.S. dollar became necessary because of a drop-off in foreign capital inflows and the appreciation of the dollar against other currencies. 

 The RBI intervened in the foreign exchange market when a "bandwagon effect" led to excessive downward pressure on the rupee, he told the Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI). 

 Consequently, he said, the rupee has remained stable at below 35 to the dollar for the past five weeks and the forward premium has started coming down, he said.

title: STATEMENT BY INDIAN FINANCE MINISTER MANMOHAN SINGH.
text:
Following is the text of a statement by Indian Finance Minister Manmohan Singh in the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Indian parliament, on the recent fall in the value of the rupee against the dollar. 


						     -----oOo-----


 In recent weeks there has been concern over the movement in the exchange rate of the rupee. After a prolonged period of stability between March 1993 and July 1995, the exchange rate of the rupee against the U.S. dollar depreciated by 10 percent between end-July 1995 and November 29, 1995. I would like to put these matters in a proper perspective. 

 All over the world, countries have shifted away from the older system of maintaining fixed exchange rates to more flexible systems in which the exchange rate is not rigidly fixed but moves from day reflecting market conditions. 

 India moved to this system in March 1993, when the earlier dual exchange rate regime was unified into a single, market-determined exchange rate system. Under this system there is no officially fixed exchange rate of the rupee. 

 Instead, the rate is determined by demand and supply conditions in the foreign exchange market while the Reserve Bank of India stands ready to intervene to maintain orderly market conditions and to curb excessive speculation. 

 Despite the shift to a market-determined system, the rupee-dollar rate remained steady at about 31.5 rupees for over two years after March 1993 until July 1995. This happened mainly because there was a large inflow of foreign portfolio investment in 1993 and most of 1994. 

 If the rupee had been left to be determined solely by the market supply and demand for foreign exchange in this period, it would have appreciated sharply against the dollar. This would have hurt exports and encouraged imports. 

 . 

 HIGHER FOREX RESERVES 

 It was therefore decided to prevent appreciation and the Reserve Bank of India intervened by buying dollars in the market. Between March 1993 and December 1994, $13 billion were added to the country's foreign currency reserves because of this process. 

 Towards the end of 1994, the inflow of portfolio investment slowed down considerably, and the upward pressure on the rupee from this source was eliminated. 

 The economy also picked up strongly in 1994/95, with industry growing at eight percent, a strong revival of investment and an overall GDP growth of 6.2 percent. 

 It was expected that the revival of the economy would generate a larger demand for imports and the balance of payments deficit on the current account would widen. This is exactly what happened. The current account deficit increased from abnormally low level of 0.1 percent of GDP in 1993/94 to 0.7 percent in 1994/95. 

 It is expected to increase further to about 1.5 percent of GDP in 1995/96. 

 This is a normal level of current account deficit in our circumstances and is sustainable by medium and long term capital inflows. 

 The reduction in capital inflows and the widening of the current account deficit ended the earlier period of surplus dollar availability. Against this background, the operation of normal supply and demand conditions in the foreign exchange markets gave rise to expectations of a depreciation of the exchange rate. 

 The exchange rate behaviour in recent months was a response to these expectations, though the extent of fluctuations was accentuated by speculative factors. 

 I would like to emphasise that despite the uncertainty created by fluctuations in the exchange rate, the overall direction of the movement of the exchange rate is consistent with the longer term objective of a viable balance of payments based on strong competitiveness of our exports. 

 One of the fundamental factors which undoubtedly influenced the movement in the exchange rate after the middle of 1995 was the fact that during the prolonged period of stability of the rupee-dollar rate from March 1993 to July 1995, our competitiveness in international markets was significantly eroded by the rate of inflation being higher than the rates of inflation of our major trading partners. 

 As a result, the index of the real effective exchange rate, which is obtained by adjusting the index of nominal effective exchange rate (using a basket of major currencies) by the differential rates of inflation (in India as compared to these major currencies) showed an appreciation of India's exchange rate in real terms in the order of seven percent between 1993-94 and August 1995. 

 This led to some erosion India's competitiveness. Had it continued, it would have adversely affected exports, the foreign trade balance and the overall balance of payments. 

 The market-triggered adjustment in the exchange rate which occurred after August 1995 led to an exchange rate which at present levels brings the real effective exchange rate back to approximately the same level as for 1993-94. 

 In other words, the recent change in the exchange rate has corrected the erosion in competitiveness and will help ensure that export growth remains strong and import growth is contained. Both factors will help to contain the trade deficit to manageable levels. 

 . 

 RBI ROLE 

 I would like to say a few words on the role of the Reserve Bank during the recent exchange rate volatility. As I have mentioned the role of the central monetary authority in modern exchange markets is to ensure orderly market conditions and to counter undue speculation. 

 From April 1993 to October 1994 the Reserve Bank intervened to prevent undue appreciation of the rupee. Thereafter purchases by the Reserve Bank was small. 

 Initially, the normal forces of demand and supply ensured that the rupee-dollar rate remained stable despite the tapering off of purchases by the Reserve Bank. 

 However, these very factors subsequently led to pressure on the exchange rate, leading to depreciation of the rupee. Initially , the downward movemnt in the rupee did not warrant any intervention by the RBI in view of the need to correct the real appreciation that had taken place since 1993/94. 

 However, as often happens when the rate changes after a long period of staticity, the change in the exchange rate triggered some speculative factors which, if unchecked, would have caused excessive depreciation. 

 Therefore, the Reserve Bank intervened decisively when the exchange rate of the rupee reached 35.80 rupees per US dollar in late October, 1995. As a result the rupee bounced back and has remained stable since then between 34.50 and 35 rupees per dollar. 

 The Reserve Bank of India will continue to monitor exchange market developments and intervene as necessary to ensure that market fluctuations are contained within reasonable levels and are consistent with economic fundamentals. 

 However, we must recognise that the world has moved away from fixed exchange rates and we should expect the exchange rate to vary in response to economic fundamentals. The real economy of the country, judging by the growth of national income, agricultural and industrial production, employment and exports, remains strong and resilent. 

 (c) Reuters Limited 1995

title: Indian Rupee Weakens Slightly Despite RBI  Intervention
text:
NEW DELHI (AP-DJ)--The Indian rupee weakened slightly Tuesday despite repeated intervention by the Reserve Bank of India through the day, and traders said premiums for forward dollars rose in volatile foreign exchange markets. 

 Meanwhile, money market rates also closed higher Tuesday, and money dealers said that the market looks ready to go up again Wednesday. 

 Vigorous month-end demand for the U.S. currency continued to bolster the dollar, despite strong intervention by the central bank. 

 However, foreign exchange dealers predicted that the rupee would bounce back later in the week as dollars from foreign telecom companies that must pay license fees to the government begin to flow in. 

 The dollar was trading at 34.93 rupees at 1140 GMT, up from 34.92 rupees at late trading Monday, but down from Tuesday morning's rate of 34.96 rupees, where the RBI first sold dollars. 

 'The RBI spread the market liberally with dollars,' Tuesday, a foreign exchange dealer at a European bank said. He noted, however, that the intervention brought the dollar down only for a short while, as there was enough corporate demand for the U.S. currency to rebound within the hour. 

 Forward premiums on six-month dollars rose to 2.73 rupees around 1140 GMT, up from 2.55 rupees at the opening and higher than 2.50 rupees-2.60 rupees Monday.

title: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 21.
text:
Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by New Delhi-based Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd. Telephone no. 11-332-4842, Fax 91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com X.400

		    TOP STORIES


 The Hindustan Times 

 PRIME MINISTER SEEKS REPORT CARD ON DEVELOPMENTAL SCHEMES 

 In a move to step up the government's anti-poverty programmes, an important election plank of the Congress, the Prime Minister's Office has asked seven development-related ministries to submit report cards on central schemes by the 10th of every month. In a series of review meetings over the last 10 days, Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao has indicated to government planners he was attaching top priority to various pro-poor schemes. 

 ----- 

 SHINDE, AHMED PATEL URGED TO BE STATE CONGRESS CHIEFS 

 The Pradesh Congress Executive Committees of the states of Maharashtra and Gujarat are expected to be announced shortly along with the new state Congress (PCC) presidents for the two states. All India Congress Committee general secretaries Sushil Kumar Shinde and Ahmed Patel are being persuaded to take over as PCC presidents in above states respectively. However, sources said both Shinde and Patel were not very keen to shift to state politics at this juncture when parliamentary elections are drawing near. 

 ----- 

 The Times Of India 

 CENTRE SAYS HELPLESS IN BREAKING MAFIA, POLITICIAN NEXUS 

 The government admitted there was a nexus between politicians, bureaucrats, individual criminals and the mafia but expressed its helplessness in improving the situation in view of the constitutional restrictions. Additional solicitor general Altaf Ahmand made this disclosure during the hearing of a public interest petition by Dinesh Trivedi, MP, seeking the Supreme Court's indulgence in getting the Vohra committee recommendations implemented. 

 ----- 

 The Pioneer 

 CIVIL CODE ONLY IF MINORITIES AGREE - HOME MINISTER 

 Union Home Minister S.B. Chavan declared that a uniform civil code would not be introduced if the minorities were not in favour of it. Addressing the Parliamentary Consultative Committee of the Home Ministry, Chavan assured the government would not allow the destruction of any religious places. The assurance followed a verbal clash among the members after BJP member V.K. Malhotra declared that Babri Masjid's demolition may be a matter of shame for "you", but for the BJP it was a matter of national pride. 


		    -----oOo-----
		    MAIN BUSINESS STORIES



The Economic Times



BANKS ASKED TO FURNISH DAILY FOREX POSITION REPORT



The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has instructed all commercial banks in the country to report their foreign exchange transactions on a daily basis. The directive was made effective from November 18. The banks have been told to spell out the buying and selling of foreign currency both for spot and forward transactions. Besides, they are required to disclose the merchant deals related to exports and imports and the size of the inter-bank cover operations.



-----



CORPORATE SECTOR GROWTH IN EXPORTS LOWER THAN IMPORTS



Exports by the corporate sector during 1994-95 grew at a lower rate than imports and domestic sales. This has resulted in a stagnancy in export intensity (exports as a percentage of net sales) at the cost of loss of net foreign exchange due to higher growth of imports of raw materials. According to a study Export Performance of Companies in the Corporate Sector 1993-94 and 1994-95, prepared by the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India, while the corporate sector's exports grew by 25.8 percent in the previous financial year, domestic sales jumped by 27 percent.



-----



ORISSA MINING CO LISTS 11 FOREIGN COS FOR GOLD, DIAMOND JVS



The Orissa government owned Orissa Mining Corporation (OMC) has shortlisted 11 foreign companies to float joint ventures for the exploration and mining of gold and diamond in the state. The overseas companies are now making a presentation before an official committee. For gold mining, OMC has shortlisted seven foreign companies, sources said. They are Gold Mines, Gold Fields Ltd, Niguni Mining, all from Australia, Malaysia Mining Corporation, Kuala Lampur, High River Mines Ltd and Kilburn Engineering pacific Ltd of Canada and Inter Continental Business Development Ltd of United Kingdom.



-----



Financial Express



CHRYSLER 800 TO TAKE ON MARUTI CAR



The US auto-giant Chrysler is keen to launch a 800 cc car in the Indian automobile market. According to industry sources, a top-level Chrysler team is to survey and subsequently prepare a project report on the automobile market. Significantly, the company's technology centre has already developed a prototype small car model which is expected to take on the Maruti 800.



-----



RBI PUMPS IN 36 BILLION RUPEES AS CALL RATE DIPS TO 20 PCT



The Reserve Bank of India intervened in the call-money market with repos of 36 billion via the apex body's agencies - the Discount and Finance House of India (DF&HI) and the Securities Trading Corporation of India (STCI). In the inter-bank call-market trades started at 30-37 percent, higher than last weekend's closing at 30 percent threabouts. Following the central bank intervention, call-rates fell to 25 percent level and finally closed at lower than 20 percent. The fall in call-rates to 20 percent comes after a long period of heavy turbulence in call-rates.



-----



INCENTIVES BY POWER MINISTRY TO WOO INDEPENDENT PRODUCERS



The Power Ministry has risen from its slumber to provide a realistic supportive framework to spur investments in projects, being pursued by Independent Power Producers (IPPs), by a series of measures announced in the last four weeks. The policy statements, coupled with proposed review of progress made in fast-track power projects by Prime Minister P.V.Narasimha Rao, demonstrates that the government is keen on encouraging at least a couple of promoters to achieve financial closure for three projects, which are under various stages of negotiation.



-----



TELECOM COM. TO REWORK RESERVE PRICES FOR BASIC SERVICES



The Telecom Commission is reworking the reserve price for fresh bidding in the 10 telecom circles for basic services where the earlier bids were rejected as unreasonable. Telecom Commission chairman R.K.Takkar said the reworking is being done in the light of industry's suggestions in this matter. Among other things, he said, a note on the restructuring of Department of Telecommunications (DoT) will be placed before the Cabinet for approval. He refuted the charge that DoT was slowing down expansion.



-----



Business Standard



PROPOSAL TO RAISE PETROLEUM PRODUCT PRICES TURNED DOWN



The Prime Minister's Office is learnt to have shot down an inter-ministerial proposal to raise retail prices of petroleum products. The price increase is expected to be effected only after the elections. The proposal was mooted in view of the depreciation of the rupee by almost 10 percent since the beginning of September and its resultant impact on the oil pool account. It was pointed out that the oil import bill for the current financial year would be around $6.75 billion as against $5.94 billion during 1994-95. The rupee value of these imports will rise in a more pronounced manner to 225 billion rupees from 178.38 billion rupees, an in increase of 261 percent.



-----



HIMACHAL FUTURISTIC TOLD TO PICK CIRCLES



The Department of Telecommunication has written to Himachal Futuristic Bezeq Communication asking it to convey the choice of the three A and B category circles it wants to retain out of the eight where it has emerged the highest bidder in the basic services tenders opened on August 31. The company has been given time till November 22 to convey its decision.



-----



OPPENHEIMER FUND TO INVEST IN UNLISTED STOCKS



Oppenheimer, the frontline American foreign institutional investor, has mopped up $150 million in its recently-launched dedicated fund aimed at investing in unlisted Indian stocks. The fund, called India Equity Fund, will invest in stocks which are in the pre-initial public offer stage, and will hold them over a 12 to 24-month time frame.



-----



WORLD BANK WANTS IMPORT CURBS LIFTED



A World Bank study says India has done a lot to open up its economy but has not removed restrictions on import of consumer goods. The study, authored by Nader Majid of the International Economics Department of the Bank's international trade division, said dismantling remaining barriers would help India and other countries in the region gain from the market opportunities in the post-Uruguay Round. Removing the remaining barriers would open up an estimated $7 billion (in 1992 dollar terms) a year in income gains, which would increase regional GDP by 2 percent and real wages by 2.5 percent.



-----



The Observer



RESERVE BANK'S PRIORITY TO CHECK PRICE RISE: RANGARAJAN



Reserve Bank Governor C.Rangarajan reiterated that the overriding concern of the monetary policy for 1995-96 would be to contain inflationary tendencies, but assured that credit would be available for productive purposes. The monetary policy would take into account the requirement of credit to support accelerated growth and also the prime objective of price stability. The nationalised banks will need to introduce innovative products while gearing up to face competition from private banks, non-banking financial companies and foreign banks in a deregulated environment, Dr Rangarajan said.



-----



Business Line



FICS, MUTUAL FUNDS COOL TO SCICI RIGHTS



Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and Indian mutual funds which collectively hold over 10 percent of the equity of SCICI Ltd, have declined to subscribe to the rights offer of the financial institution aggregating 13.11 billion rupees. FIIs, which hold around seven percent of the equity in SCICI, have decided to ignore the offering, given the depressed state of the capital market and the prospects of the company. Apart from Unit Trust of India, the response from other mutual funds to the issue has been lukewarm. The decision of FIIs not to subscribe to the offering has been attributed to the fact that it is a PCN (partly convertible note) issue.



-----



PETROLEUM SECTOR DRAFT POLICY RUNS INTO TROUBLE



The Petroleum Ministry may have to tone down its proposed exploration and production policy considerably in the face of the strong reservations being expressed by the national oil companies and experts. The draft policy, in a bid to step up exploration effort and attract private sector interest, proposes radical changes such as PSU participation in bidding rounds, an open-acreage system with offers being evaluated on a quarterly basis and contracts awarded in three months, reduction of royalty and abolition of cess. However, the public sector companies, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India Ltd (OIL), are opposed to the draft policy on various counts, say government sources.

title: (AWSJ): India Banks Expected To Raise Prime Lending Rate
text:
BOMBAY (AP-DJ)--Commercial banks in India are expected to raise their prime lending rates by about one percentage point within the next week, bankers and analysts say, Friday's Asian Wall Street Journal reports. 

 They cite sharp increases in short-term interest rates, rising term-deposit rates and higher demand for credit from industry. 

 Since January, banks have already raised their prime rates - those charged on loans to their best customers - by one to two percentage points, to an average of 16% to 16.5%. Other corporate borrowers get funds at 18% to 19%. 

 The immediate trigger for a prime increase is a sharp climb in interbank overnight call rates, the rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. Overnight call rates hit a high of 85% last Friday, dropped back down to about 50% earlier this week and spiked upward again Thursday. 

 Reserve Bank of India intervention since mid-October to support the rupee, which has fallen about 10% against the U.S. dollar since mid-August, sucked rupees out of the banking system and pushed overnight rates sharply higher from less than 20% previously. 

 The central bank has spent an estimated $500 million to $700 million supporting the currency by buying rupees in the foreign-exchange market. 

 Foreign banks are expected to lead the way in raising prime rates. With few branches and limited domestic-deposit bases, foreign banks are more sensitive to changes in interbank rates. 

 'There has been a rise in deposit rates. We will see their impact on the lending rates. We see a clear case for a one percentage point rise in prime rates,' says Ravi Nursey, treasury head at Dresdner Bank AG in Bombay.

 The Times of India 

 UNITED STATES MAY GIVE PAKISTAN MORE ARMS 

 External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee has said the government is evolving a befitting response at the diplomatic and military levels to what he feels is a resumption of the United States' arms supplies to Pakistan. He said that even though the U.S. had said that this was a one-time waiver, the possibility of the latter giving more arms to Pakistan had not been ruled out. 

 Indian Express 

 RUPEE WILL NOT FALL FURTHER SAYS COMMERCE MINISTER 

 Allaying fears of a continuing downside of the rupee, Commerce Minister, P.Chidambaram asserted that the recent fall was no more than a correction and that the rupee could only appreciate hereafter. He said the Reserve Bank of India, the central bank, would strongly intervene to stem any speculative run on the value of the rupee and advised exporters not to hold back their earnings and importers against any panic accumulation of the dollar. 

 The Economic Times 

 SEBI MAY INTRODUCE LOCK-IN PERIOD FOR BOUGHT-OUT DEALS 

 The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) may introduce a lock-in period for issues placed through the bought-out route. This means the investment bankers who acquire shares from new promoters for subsequently issuing them to general investors though an offer for sale, will have to hold these shares for a certain interval. SEBI believes the investment bankers must take the risk for some time, before they can pass on the shares to public investors. The reason for such a move is to restrict investment bankers from bringing to the capital market issues which lack credibility. 

 FOREIGN INVESTMENT PROMOTION BOARD OKAYS 23 BLN RUPEE 

 REFINERY IN UTTAR PRADESH

The joint venture will have a foreign equity portion of around 5.98 billion rupees. The six-million-tonne green field refinery is expected to come up at Sultanpur. Shell already has an agreement with Bharat Petroleum to sell its lubricants in India. 

 APRIL-SEPTEMBER TRADE DEFICIT UP AT $2,380 MLN

However, the monthly increase in the deficit rate has shown a decline since July 1995 and further moderation is expected in the second-half of the current year. Releasing India's foreign trade figures for the first six months of the current fiscal, Minister of State for Commerce P.Chidambaram, said the month-over-month increase in the trade deficit, which peaked at $702 million in July, had dipped to $409 million in September.

The committee has been given three months time, and sources said the status papers on various industries, currently under reservation, were under preparation. 

 MORGAN STANLEY SOLICITS OFFERS FOR $1-B OMAN-INDIA PIPELINE 

 EQUITY 

 Morgan Stanley, investment banker for the Oman Oil Company, is preparing an offer document to raise $1 billion as equity for the Oman-India pipeline project. The offer, for participation in the ownership consortium of the $4-billion project, will be made to global energy majors as well as strategic and institutional investors. Gas Authority of India Limited (G.A.I.L.), the Indian gas distribution partner, will also be offered a part of the equity. However, it is uncertain whether G.A.I.L. will pick up the stake. 

 RENEGOTIATIONS WITH ENRON SLATED FOR NOVEMBER 1. 

 The Maharashtra government will hold renegotiations with the U.S. multinational, Enron, on the Dabhol power project on November 1 as per the conditions laid down by right wing Shiv Sena chief Bal Thackeray. The committee for renegotiation would be appointed within a few days and would comprise only experts and the concerned secretaries. No minister would be included in the renegotiation committee.  ESCORTS PLANS CONSORTIA TO BID FOR INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS 

 The 22 billion rupees Escorts group is planning to form a consortia, with leading international players, to bid for major infrastructure development projects. Arvind N Agrawal, executive director, Escorts Construction Equipment Ltd and head of Escorts Construction Equipment Business Group, said Escorts will bid for a number of projects including port modernisation and airport development projects, commercial and industrial parks as well as bypasses and bridges. 

 Financial Express 

 WORLD BANK REPORT FINDS PUBLIC SECTOR MEMORANDUM OF 

 UNDERSTANDING SYSTEM INEFFECTIVE 

 The World Bank has dumped the Memorandum of Understanding system in public sector undertakings as ineffective in improving the return on assets, labour productivity and total factor productivity of the companies. The bank has faulted the Indian Government and public managers for setting flawed targets resulting in lowering of total factor productivity (T.F.P.) to below pre-contract levels. According to a World Bank paper, T.P.F. measures the efficiency with which all factors are used and is the most reliable indicator of whether the contracts were associated with performance improvements. 

 RESERVE BANK PLANS BIG PUSH TO PROP UP RUPEE 

 Haunted by the looming spectre of a Mexico-type crisis, the Reserve Bank of India has put together a megaplan to crush increasing speculation in the foreign exchange markets and prop up the rupee. The big push which is expected to be put into action on Monday has been conceived in concert with the top mandarins of the Ministry of Finance. The intervention has been designed to aim at propping up the rupee from the current level of 35.60 and keep it between 33.50 and 34.00 to the dollar.

 GUIDELINES FOR TAKEOVER OF OLD POWER PLANTS ANNOUNCED 

 In a bid to augment availability of power in a quicker and cheaper way, the government has formulated detailed guidelines for private participation for renovation and modernisation of thermal and hydel power projects. The guidelines envisage three options which include lease, rehabilitate, operate and transfer, sale of plant and joint venture between state electricity boards and private companies. 

 FINANCE FIRMS WITHOUT RATING FACE ACTION 

 Almost 65 percent of non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), of 20 million rupees and above and registered with the Reserve Bank of India, may face deregisteration for not complying with the directive obliging them to obtain a credit rating. Notwithstanding the extension of the deadline, only 110 of the 312 registered large NBFCs have so far undergone a credit rating for their deposit scheme through an approved credit rating agency, as stipulated by the central bank. 

 MINING INDUSTRY MOST LUCRATIVE FOR OVERSEAS INVESTMENT 

 Price Waterhouse, the international financial audit and management consultancy firm, has identified the Indian mining industry as the most lucrative area of investment for overseas mining and exploration companies. The World Mining Group (W.M.G.), the specialised Price Waterhouse arm that provides a wide range of services to mining industries on a global scale, will soon prepare a detailed report on the country's prospects for circulation among its clients. W.M.G. chairman Robert B Parsons said the audit firm is particularly keen to guide foreign mining interests to India's geological resources.

 Multinational telecom giants AT&T and US-West are lobbying with the Prime Minister's Office to be awarded licences for providing cellular mobile services. Both the companies - along with their Indian partners, Birla and BPL - are trying to get minimum of three licences in category 'A' and 'B'. A Department of Telecom official said both the companies favoured no cap on cellular service licences but, due to political implications, they considered a cap of three.

title: India Economic Officials Bail Out Ailing Rupee: Amplifier
text:
NEW DELHI (AP-DJ)--The Indian government finally drew the line on a recent slide in the rupee against the dollar, as key officials stepped in an apparently coordinated effort to talk up the rupee and backed it up by more forceful intervention and other measures from the Reserve Bank of India. 

 After watching the rupee tumble about 12% over the past two months, officials set the stage for a rupee rebound over the weekend as Commerce Secretary P. Chidambaram told an unusual Sunday press conference that he felt the rupee had fallen too far and should rally. 

 Those sentiments were echoed in a strongly-worded statement from Reserve Bank Gov. C. Rangarajan on Monday, who described the rupee's recent weakness as a short-term disequilibrium that 'must get reversed.' 

 To that end, the central bank later announced moves it said were aimed at increasing supplies of and limiting demand for foreign exchange in the domestic market. 

 And the RBI also launched another round of intervention Monday to support the rupee, a spokeswoman for the bank confirmed. Though she wouldn't elaborate on the bank's activities, traders said the central bank took the unprecedented step of selling dollars in the forward markets as well as in the spot market.

title: India 's RBI Gov/Rupee -4: Repeats Will Continue  Intervention
text:
The RBI Governor's statement echoed comments made Sunday by Commerce Minister P. Chidambaram - who also referred to a recent drop in the rupee as an 'over-correction' - indicating that key Indian monetary officials are united in their resolve to defend the rupee. 

 The RBI also intervened to sell dollars in local markets Monday, pushing the rupee below 35.00 rupees, and the RBI Governor reiterated in his statement that the central bank will continue to do so as needed. 

 'RBI will stand ready to intervene with the objective of moderating the volatility in the exchange market while being consistent with the fundamentals,' he said. 

 Rangarajan added that expectations have played a part in the rupee's recent weakness. While importers left many of their positions uncovered during the two-years of stability, now that the rupee has fallen they have rushed to the market to cover. 

 Exporters, meanwhile, have responded by delaying the repatriation of their overseas earnings, Rangarajan noted. 

 'All these can result in a short-term dis-equilibrium between the supply and demand for foreign exchange, thus exerting a pressure on the currency. It appears such a phenomenon has been in operation in the recent period and it must get reversed,' Rangarajan said.

title: Indian government says rupee has fallen enough.
text:
NEW DELHI, Oct 29 (Reuter) - India sought to shore up a weakening rupee on Sunday with a blunt warning to foreign exchange speculators and a plea to traders to ignore predictions by some analysts that the currency will fall further. 

 Commerce Minister P. Chidambaram said the rupee, which has lost 12 percent in value against the U.S. dollar in two months, had declined too much and was poised to rebound. 

 "I think given the soundness of the fundamentals of the Indian economy, there simply is no justification for any expectation that the rupee will decline or ought to decline," Chidambaram told reporters. 

 He said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, would intervene aggressively in the foreign exchange market if speculators tried to push the rupee down more. 

 "I have every reason to believe the RBI will intervene strongly if speculative activities tend to push down the value of the rupee," Chidambaram said. 

 He said the trade picture was brightening, with exports growing strongly and a surge in imports tapering off. 

 On Friday afternoon the Indian currency traded in a narrow range of about 35.55 to the dollar, well below its level of 31.4 which had held for some two years until August. 

Central bank intervention on Friday helped take the rupee off its low of 35.72, but dealers said six-month forward dollars were quoted at more than 38 rupees. 

 Bunched debt repayments and growing oil import bills have weakened the currency. The fall gained momentum when dollar supplies thinned as the inflow of foreign funds slowed and exporters held back repatriation hoping for better rates. 

 The rupee's fall has sent shivers through Indian stock markets. Foreign institutional investors, the main buyers in the bourses in the past few months, were caught unaware by the abrupt fall in the rupee which has eroded their portfolios. 

 Chidambaram, one of the architects of Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's four-year-old economic reform programme, said the government shared his view the rupee had fallen enough. 

 "It is my view that anything beyond 34.50 (rupees per dollar) is perhaps an overcorrection," he said. "That is shared by the government, that an overcorrection may have already taken place and if anything, the rupee will appreciate." 

 Chidambaram, noting the six-month premium on the dollar was at an all-time high on Friday of almost 14 percent, appealed to importers not rush their purchases in anticipation they will soon cost more. "There is enough foreign exchange," he said. 

 He told exporters not to hold back on purchases. 

 "Exporters should bring back export earnings as soon as possible," he said. "If both importers and exporters continue to harbour these completely unjustified expectations, then the rupee will decline and both will be hurt." 

 Chidambaram said inflows of foreign direct investment and portfolio investment remained strong, and a surge in imports earlier in the year, especially of petroleum, newsprint and fertiliser, had tapered off. 

 Imports soared 50 percent in June compared with the same month in 1994, but the growth was 14 percent in September. 

 He predicted India's current account deficit would be between one and 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in the 1995/96 financial year ending next March 31, higher than 0.8 percent last year but well within manageable limits.

title: India Rupee/Stabilizes -2: Traders See Shift In RBI Tactics
text:
As trading continued into the afternoon, the Reserve Bank of India again sold dollars for rupees, the central bank confirmed. 

 The sales began after the dollar inched back to 35.60 rupees, and continued until the U.S. currency fell back to 35.50 rupees, traders said. 

 Some traders saw the Reserve Bank of India's interventions Friday as a shift in tactics. They said the RBI appeared Friday to be trying to defend the rupee at a specific level, rather than simply providing liquidity to keep the market orderly. 

 'It looks as if the whole idea is to get the dollar below a rate of 35.70-35.80 rupees,' a trader with a European bank said. 

 'The market has started respecting the Reserve bank's intervention,' another dealer said, who added that the dollar's rates could start to decline next week if players become certain that the RBI will continue to defend the currency strongly. 

 Traders noted that the RBI's seriousness could be seen in the size of the lots it sold, which increased Friday from previous days. 

 'The size of the lots is larger now... they're selling in $3 million-$5 million lots today as compared to smaller lots' of $1 million-$3 million last week, the European bank trader said.

title: India/Stock/Amplifier -2: RBI Hasn't Restored Trust
text:
Analysts note that the rupee's sudden drop - which follows nearly two years of almost unbroken stability against the dollar - has shocked many observers who had predicted only a slow and small decline in the currency this year. 

 And some half-hearted intervention from the Reserve Bank of India has done little to restore confidence, they add, noting that the central bank has only sold very small amounts of dollars that haven't managed to stop the rupee's slide. 

 Indeed, the RBI confirmed that it continued to sell dollars for rupees in local markets Thursday. Though the bank didn't comment on the size of the sales, traders who dealt with the banks said it sold just $2-3 million a trade, which wasn't enough to help lift the rupee. 

 'The problem is that the RBI is not willing to intervene in a large way,' says Ashwini Agarwal, research director at S.S. Kantilal Ishwarlal Securities. 'They don't want to dip into their reserves for short-term benefits.' 

 Most observers attribute the rupee's weakness to a surge in dollar demand from importers of capital goods and raw materials used to fuel India's strong industrial growth this year. 

 The boost in imports widened India's trade deficit to $1.976 billion in the April-August period - the first five months of the financial year, from $798.5 million in the same months of last year.

title: India: Bombay Shares Close Lower On Rupee Worries
text:
BOMBAY (AP-DJ)--Shares on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), the smaller bourse in Bombay, closed lower Tuesday as the falling value of the rupee vis-a-vis the dollar depressed sentiment, brokers said. 

 The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) is closed Tuesday and Wednesday on account of a Hindu festival. 

 The rupee, which had fallen to a low of 35.85 rupees against the dollar Friday, remained under pressure hovering around 35.55 for the better part of the day. With forex market participants describing the intervention of India's central bank, the Reserve Bank of India, as half-hearted, dealers didn't rule out a further fall in the value of the rupee. 

 The precarious position of the rupee is sending shock waves through the NSE, said a dealer from Classic Share & Stockbroking Services Ltd. 

 Foreign funds reason that they could sell their holdings and pick them back up when the rupee dwindles further. New foreign funds on the verge of entering the Indian market, may find it more attractive, but they too are watching to see where the rupee finally plateaus, said Nandkishore Gupta, chief executive of Indsec Share & Stockbroking Ltd. 

 Since several financial institutions, brokerages and the BSE weren't working Tuesday, volume on the NSE was thin. 

 'Usually institutions are around to buy when prices fall; today (Tuesday) they aren't working,' said the Classic dealer. 

 Shares of Reliance Industries Ltd. fell over 5 rupees and are expected to close at 250.50, against Monday's close of 255.75 rupees. 

 Shares of Tata Iron & Steel Co. fell 6 rupees and are expected to close at 241 rupees. 

 Gupta said trading on the NSE at a time when most of the other exchanges and institutions are closed has magnified the 'crisis-sentiment' in the equities markets, as dealers test the market with 'irresponsible' prices. The low prices on the terminals further depresses sentiment.

title: Dollar demand pushes Indian rupee to record low.
text:
BOMBAY, Oct 20 (Reuter) - A surge in demand for dollars pushed the Indian rupee to a record low of 35.70 to the dollar on Friday, defying a central bank attempt to arrest the fall, market analysts said. 

 "The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened (sold dollars) at the 35.30 and the 35.50 level but it didn't have any impact," said a dealer at a Bombay bank. 

 Analysts said a slowdown in foreign currency inflows into the country precipitated the rupee's fall. 

 The currency closed afternoon trading at 35.60. It has lost almost 12 percent in value in two months. 

 While most bank dealers felt that the rupee would continue to slide if current dollar demand persisted, investment analysts said the current fall was not a long-term trend. 

 "There is no depth in these movements," said Ramnath Iyer, analyst at Peregrine Capital in Bombay. "This is the result of a short-term mismatch," he said. 

 Bank dealers said there was an all-round rise in demand for dollars from Indian corporates for imports and debt repayments before December, the end of the financial year for many international firms. 

 "The devaluation in currency value was expected as Indian exporters wanted to be compensated for the inflation in the domestic sector," said an analyst with an Indian brokerage. 

 "The fall has been mainly because of an imbalance in currency flows during the first half of the year," said an analyst with WI Carr, the broking arm of Banque Indosuez. 

 Imports in the first half of 1995/96 (April to March) rose 39 percent while exports grew by 29 percent from a lower base. "The resulting deficit led to demand for the dollar," he said. 

 Debt repayments of the government and a few corporates due for the second quarter of 1995/96 made the imbalance worse. 

 Last year, when foreign exchange inflows were high, the RBI had intervened to prevent the rupee from appreciating. But this year, the RBI has intervened only sporadically to limit the fall, encouraging dealers to believe the central bank supported a gradual devaluation. 

 Some analysts believe the rupee will strengthen. 

 "The rupee can only strengthen from the current level," said Iyer of Peregrine Capital. 

 WI Carr also said it expected dollar inflows to improve in the second the half of current fiscal, strengthening the rupee in the process.

title: Indian rupee range-bound on RBI  intervention  fear.
text:
BOMBAY, Oct 18 (Reuter) - The Indian rupee traded in a narrow band between 34.80-34.97 per dollar on Wednesday in a market where players were looking over their shoulders to see if the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) would intervene, dealers said. 

 "Throughout the morning, the market was worried that RBI would intervene above the 34.90 rupee level," a dealer said. As a result, many sold at 34.80 level for fear of intervention. 

 "It (34.90) became a psychological barrier," said a dealer. The recent intervention by the central bank to arrest the Indian rupee's slide was to bring stability to the market, said Shankar Acharya, a senior finance ministry official in New Delhi. 

 But a few bankers said they knew RBI would not intervene at 34.90, the level at which it intervened on Monday. "The rates were not that volatile today," said a dealer. 

 "On Monday, the rupee fell by almost one rupee without large volumes being traded," said another dealer. "Today the movement was slow, and the market demand is more than what RBI can sell." 

 A dealer at a state-run bank said the highest level at which the dollar was sold was 34.96 and the lowest was 34.75. 

 "If the same trend continues, the dollar could touch the 36.0 rupee level by December," said Dayanand Nayak, chief forex dealer at Corporation Bank. 

 A treasury manager with a city company said capital goods imports by many corporates had to be paid up before December end, the financial year closing of most international firms. 

 A leading Indian oil firm was also in the market for dollars to pay for large petroleum imports, dealers said. 

 "RBI can't sell heavily to prop up the rupee without affecting its reserves," he said.

title: Indian Rupee Opens Slightly Stronger; No Sign Of RBI
text:
NEW DELHI (AP-DJ)--The Indian rupee opened slightly stronger in slow early trading Wednesday, with fear of intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) keeping trading extremely thin and cautious, dealers said.

 At 0500 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 34.80 rupees, just below the 34.90 rupee level struck in late trading Tuesday. On Monday, the RBI began selling dollars at 34.90 rupees, and continued to about 34.40 rupees.

The Times of India


 SUPREME COURT GRANTS BAIL TO SANJAY DUTT 

 Film star Sanjay Dutt, who has been imprisoned for more than 15 months at Bombay's high-security Arthur Road jail, has been granted bail by the Supreme Court. Sources said that a letter regarding this was sent to the government after the Election Commission had elicited the views of all the recognised political parties.

 ALL-PARTY MEET TO DISCUSS KASHMIR POLLS 

 The government has convened an all-party meeting on election prospects in Jammu and Kashmir and cancelled the leave of its employees to ensure their availability for poll duty in the terrorism-affected state. This marked a step-up in the government's preparations for holding elections in the state before December 15 and coincided with a resumed effort by the ruling Congress party high command to patch up differences between the rival factions of its state unit.

 INDO-U.S. TALKS ON SCIENCE AND TECHOLOGY BREAK DOWN AGAIN 

 Discussions between India and the United States on the umbrella Indo-U.S. Agreement on Science and Techology have once again broken down, putting into jeopardy a wide range of accords on energy between the two countries. The recent round of discussions were held between senior officials of the Indian Department of Science and Technology and a U.S. delegation led by Special Advisor to the President and Senior Director for Global Affairs on the National Security Council.

SELECTED COMPANIES ASKED TO DISCLOSE END-USE OF ISSUE FUNDS

AES Transpower Director Tony Colman is leading a team of power experts to renegotiate the power purchase agreement (P.P.A.) with the government of the eastern Indian state of Orissa. CENTRAL BANK INTERVENES TO KEEP RUPEE AFLOAT AGAINST DOLLAR


India's central bank, the Reserve Bank of India (R.B.I.), intervened in the foreign exchange market as the rupee touched a low of 34.90 against the dollar. NEW SYSTEM OF EXPORT IMPORT CLASSIFICATION RELEASED

Spectrum Power is the first fast track power developer which has offered to go ahead with its plant without a counter-guarantee. The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) has sought an extension of the external commercial borrowing approval it has secured from the Ministry of Finance for in June.

The Finance Ministry has joined the Reserve Bank of India in arm-twisting public sector banks into buying government paper. The ministry has directed most public sector banks to bail out the 30 billion rupee 13.5 percent, two year maturity paper issued on October 14.

title: India  RBI  intervenes  to arrest rupee's fall vs dlr.
text:
BOMBAY, Oct 16 (Reuter) - The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday interevened to prevent the rupee from falling to a low of 35 rupees per dollar, reassuring worried importers and encouraging exporters to sell the U.S. currency, dealers said. 

 "It is the first time they have intervened to push up the rupee," said a dealer with a private bank. "Until now, we've heard about interventions only through state-run banks." 

 "They had to send a signal to the market," said a dealer at a state-run bank, referring to panic among importers rushing for forward cover at high premia after the rupee showed signs of continuing weakness over the last few weeks. 

 "The market was moving in one way only -- importers panicking and exporters postponing sale of dollars hoping that the rupee would fall further," he said. 

 The premia on forward dollars touched a high of 9.0 percent annualised from around 7.0 percent last month, dealers said. 

 An RBI official confirmed reports that the central bank sold dollars at around 34.0/34.15 level to arrest the fall of rupee which had touched a low of 34.90, threatening to touch the 35.0 rupees per dollar level. She declined to elaborate further. 

 Analysts had predicted in September that the rupee would continue its downhill slide, weakened by a strong growth in imports coupled with lower foreign investments this year. 

 "Too much depreciation can make imports expensive and push up inflation, and RBI doesn't want that," said a dealer. 

 Dealers said the rupee opened at 34.20/25 on Monday and steadily weakened to touch a low of 34.95. 

 "At that level, there was some profit-booking, and the rupee moved marginally up to 34.90," said a dealer. 

 "All of a sudden, the dollar crashed to 34.0 and the rupee held on at that level for some time," said another dealer. 

 After the RBI intervention, the rupee weakened again to the 34.60/90 level showing genuine demand from corporates for the U.S. currency. 

 "It doesn't mean the RBI move was unsuccessful," said a dealer. "But for their intervention, the rupee would have fallen below the 35 level," he said. 

 "Last time, it was fear and speculative pressure," said a dealer, explaining the rupee's fall to 35.0 per dollar in end-September. 

 "This time it is genuine corporate cover," she said. "It is even more dangerous." 

 When the rupee plunged to an all-time low of 35 to the dollar in September, RBI did not intervene. The local currency recovered marginally to settle around the 34.0 per dollar level. 

 Dealers and even exporters appreciated the RBI action. "It is good they have shown some initiative," said the treasury manager of a steel company. 

 He said Indian corporates were not educated enough to cope with such volatility in the exchange rate. 

 "If they don't smoothen the market, who else will?" asked another dealer. "Last time they left it to market forces and were rapped by the press," he said, referring to the fall of rupee against the dollar in end-September.

title: India rupee at record low, then recovers.
text:
BOMBAY, Sept 15 (Reuter) - The Indian rupee plunged to a record low against the dollar on Friday but recovered marginally even though the central bank refused to intervene, leaving the currency to seek its natural level, bankers said. 

 The rupee hit the 35 rupee per dollar level on Friday morning before rebounding to 34 rupees on rumours of a planned intervention by the central Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 

 The local currency recovered to fluctuate between 33.25 and 34.25 through the afternoon, although there was no official intervention by the central bank. 

 However, RBI officials said they were keeping "a very close watch" on the currrency. 

 Bankers said in the near-term the rupee would not cross the 35-rupee level as most importers stayed away after the local currency hit the all-time low in the morning. 

 "It looks like the rupee will trade in the range of 32-35 per dollar in the near future," said Rajendra Gill, treasury head with Bank of Nova Scotia in Bombay. 

 "But there will be a net demand for the dollars in the next few months," he added. 

 Bankers said the RBI was probably testing the waters before India introduces further currency relaxations. The rupee was made convertible on the current account in August last year, but the RBI has retained several restrictions on capital movement. 

 "The RBI is letting the rupee find its level since it goes well with its policy of liberalisation and as the rupee finally depreciates it gives exporters some incentive," one dealer said. 

 Bankers said that the sudden depreciation could create nervousness in the market. Although RBI stayed out of the market, they felt it could use "moral suasion" to cool sentiment. 

 "How can one remain unconcerned," a central bank official told Reuters when asked if the central bank was planning to prevent a further fall of the rupee. 

 Indian finance secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia, the top civil servant in the finance ministry, said the fall is "just a normal market situation". He told Reuters: "I don't see any problem really." 

 The rupee, which was at 31.40 to the dollar about a month ago, began to slide after the Indian government said it would raise its entire requirement of foreign debt payments through the inter-bank foreign exchange market. 

 Dealers said as most exporters had already sold their receivables forward, the immediate dollar supply was limited. 

 But analysts said foreign portfolio investments will not be adversely affected. 

 "It won't make much of a difference," said analyst Ramnath Iyer, with Peregrine Capital in Bombay. "Foreign funds expect 5-6 percent currency depreciation when they invest abroad." 

 In real terms the rupee had appreciated in the past two years because it has held steady, he said. 

 "The fall now is more like a correction," Iyer said. "It is not a devaluation in the Mexican sense. We expect the rupee to stabilise between 33.2 and 33.5." 

 Most industry analysts welcomed the depreciation of the rupee. 

 "The impact should be beneficial for Indian industry in general because it will provide extra protection against imports," said R. Balakrishnan, head of research with DSP Financial Consultants, an Indian associate of Merrill Lynch. 

 "Foreign portfolio investment could rise as Indian stocks look cheaper in dollar terms," Balakrishnan said.

title: India 's RBI may  intervene  to support rupee - dealers.
text:
BOMBAY, Sept 14 (Reuter) - The Indian rupee could get some support from the central bank after the local currency crossed the psychological barrier of 33 per dollar in early trade. 

 "Under the Reserve Bank of India's laws, the central bank is supposed to either change its buying and selling rate for the dollar or keep the rupee within a five percent band of these rates," one dealer said. 

 "The RBI is very likely to intervene," the dealer said. 

 The rupee has fallen by around 5.0 percent from the RBI's buying rate of 31.37 per dollar after it hit the 33 level. 

 But the central bank announced its buying and selling rates unchanged at 31.37 and 31.53 respectively. 

 RBI officials were not immediately available for comment. 

 The rupee was trading at 33.10/15 per dollar in early trade after opening nearly unchanged at 32.83/86. 

 The dealers said the rupee may have found a new support at 33 rupees per dollar but no one was sure where the local currency would stabilise. 

 The rupee has been falling against the dollar over the past fortnight mainly on dollar buying by state-run banks for the Indian government's foreign debt payments. 

 But with every fall many banks were reported to have taken speculative positions also, pushing the rupee down further. 

 "The initial nudge came from large demand for dollars from oil firms but the dollar buying for debt payments seem to have taken the bottom off," a dealer with a state-run bank said.

title: India  Reserve Bank/Rupee-Dlr -3: Not Required To  Intervene
text:
'Basically, the exchange rate reflects the economic fundamentals,' Sodhani said. He said that view still applies even after the dollar jumped sharply to a new all-time high against the rupee around 33.70 rupees Thursday, up from 32.87 Wednesday. 

 After two years of almost unbroken stability for the rupee, a surge in importer demand and a slowdown in investment inflows has pushed the rupee sharply lower in recent days, with the currency falling about 6% against the dollar since the end of August. 

 Sodhani noted that although the Reserve Bank has previously intervened to prevent an appreciation of the rupee that could harm Indian exporters, it hasn't stepped in to block a depreciation. 

 He also noted that the central bank isn't bound by law to defend the currency at any specific level, as some local press reports have erroneously suggested. 

 'There is no question of the Reserve Bank (being required to) intervene if the rate moves more than 5%,' he said. 

 But he declined to elaborate further on the bank's position on future intervention, however. 

 'When the central bank should intervene and when it will not is not something a central bank announces in advance,' he said.

 TOP STORIES 

 The Hindustan Times 

 BEANT SINGH'S ASSASSIN IDENTIFIED; TWO ARRESTED 

 Police say they have unearthed a deadly plot behind the assassination of Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh. Two people -- an engineer of a private firm, who designed the human bomb, and a Punjab police constable -- have been arrested in this connection. The identity of the person who is believed to have been used as the human bomb has also been established.

 Indian Express 

 INDIA DENOUNCES PAKISTAN FOR POLITICISING WOMEN'S MEET 

 India has sharply denounced Pakistan for raising the Kashmir issue at the world women's conference at Beijing. India's Human Resources Development Minister Madhavrao Scindia told the second day's session of the conference in Beijing that Pakistan, instead of condemning and evolving measures to eliminate terrorism, had chosen to politicise issues by raising Kashmir. 

 ----- 

 VIOLENCE MARS AGRA STRIKE 

 N.D.Tiwari, the head of a rebel faction of India's ruling Congress party, was injured and arrested in Agra while leading a group of demonstrators in violation of prohibitory orders towards the Taj Mahal. The demonstrators were protesting against moves to relocate industries situated near the Taj Mahal. 

 ----- 


				 TOP BUSINESS STORIES



The Economic Times



CHANGES HINTED AT IN POWER POLICY TO ELIMINATE GREY AREAS



The government plans major changes in its power policy, including the abolition of two-part tariffs, removal of assured returns on equity and minimum plant-load factors, a fixed time frame for project execution, foreign equity returns and protection of foreign debt servicing from forex fluctuations and mandatory fuel-based bidding. Union Power Minister N.K.P. Salve said the ministry would soon constitute an expert committee to help frame the amended power policy. Competitive bidding on projects with fixed single tariff as the only criteria will remove all possibilities of capital cost padding, he added.



-----



NEW CENTRAL DEPOSITORY NORM GETS GOVERNMENT APPROVAL



The cabinet has decided to bring forward legislation to set up a central depository in securities. The depository will provide computerised book-entry of securities, enabling transfer of ownership based on delivery of securities against payment of cash in listed or to-be-listed companies. The service will also provide computerised book entry of pledges of securities.



-----



ENRON WILLING TO REDUCE TARIFF BY 10 PAISE PER UNIT



The Dabhol Power Co (DPC) is willing to reduce the tariff for the first-phase of its $920 million project to 2.30 rupees per unit from 2.40 rupees proposed in the power purchase agreement. A company source said by effecting a change in fuel, the tariff for the first phase could be leveled at 10 paise less, besides ruling out any escalation. DPC is also willing to give up the fuel management contract to Maharashtra State Electricity Board and induct an Indian partner with 30 percent equity stake.



-----



RESERVE BANK TO INTERVENE IF RUPEE SLIDE CONTINUES



The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is closely monitoring the slide of the rupee against the dollar as it touched this year's lowest, but there are no clear indications yet as to the level at which it will intervene. The spot dollar opened at 31.88-31.90 rupee levels on Tuesday and crossed the immediate pre-budget low of Rs 32.15 to touch Rs 32.57. RBI officials said the RBI had not resorted to any intervention and the current fluctuation in the rupee was purely on account of demand and supply factors.



-----



HONDA MOTOR TO PICK UP 51 PCT STAKE IN CAR VENTURE WITH SIEL



Honda Motor Co will pick up 51 percent equity in its proposed car joint venture with the Siddharth Sriram group's flagship, SIEL Ltd. SIEL, like DCM in its joint venture with Daewoo, will hold a minority stake in the proposed joint venture. According to sources, the Honda-SIEL car is expected to hit the road late in 1997.



-----



RESERVE BANK SEEKS HIKE IN FOREIGN EQUITY LEVEL



The Reserve Bank of India has approached the Finance Ministry to raise the foreign equity participation level from the present 51 percent to 74 percent in the case of joint ventures with foreign financial participation for automatic approval. The central bank has taken up the issue of increasing the scope for automatic approval of foreign financial collaborations and raising statutory foreign investment limits with the government.



------



Business Standard



BOURSE TIGHTENS MARGINS TO CURB PRICE RIGGING IN CASH GROUP



The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) has tightened its margin system for non-specified (cash) shares to clamp down on overtrading in B-group shares. The system comes into effect from the new settlement period starting Monday. The BSE has replaced the flat margin of 20 percent on scrip-wise net positions by a graded but tough set of margins.



-----



INDIA'S RELIANCE SETS SIGHTS ON U.S. OIL EXPLORATION COMPANY



Reliance Industries Ltd is examining the possibility of taking over a U.S. oil exploration company Santa Fe Energy. Sources said Reliance has held talks with the Houston-based company for a possible takeover. The acquisition will serve Reliance's purpose of arranging a long-term crude oil source for the 15 million tonne refinery it is setting up in India's Gujarat state.



-----



FORD, MAHINDRAS SEEK APPROVAL FOR $800 MLN VENTURE



Ford Motor Co of the U.S. and India's Mahindra & Mahindra have filed an application with Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) for approval to establish a joint venture company to manufacture Ford vehicles. The proposal envisages an investment of more than $800 million in the venture in which the two partners will hold 50 percent stakes.



-----



Financial Express



BOMBAY BOURSE TO SUSPEND TRADING IN 1,000 SCRIPS NEXT WEEK



The Bombay bourse has decided to suspend trading in nearly 1,000 companies from Monday till further notice. According to top bourse officials, these companies have failed to adhere to clause 16 of the listing agreement of the exchange which stipulates that adequate notice of book closure/record date be mentioned.



-----



The Observer of Business and Politics



ELECTRICITY BOARD EASES NORMS FOR PRIVATE PROJECT CLEARANCE



The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has streamlined its norms for faster clearance of private power projects following criticism for slow appraisal of projects. Clearance for a project may now be granted within a month of an application being filed. The techno-economic clearance would take about two months.



-----



FIRE TEST MUST FOR RAYONS



A flammability test certificate will be mandatory for all rayon chiffon garments exported from India including skirts, blouses, dresses and scarves. Textile Secretary T.S.R. Subramaniam said the rule was extended to scarves as the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission recently confirmed that 100 percent chiffon scarves had not met the U.S. government's flamability standards.



-----



DELHI BOURSE TO BRING ALL NORTHERN BOURSES UNDER ONE UMBRELLA



The Delhi bourse plans to bring all bourses in the northern region under one umbrella in an attempt to boost liquidity and business of its member-brokers. According to the plan, Delhi bourse members would be allowed to give terminals to their counterparts of other stock exchanges, who will deal on sub-terminals of original members.

title: India  panel favours selective RBI  intervention .
text:
BOMBAY, July 7 (Reuter) - A committee set up by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on foreign exchange market reforms said it favoured selective central bank intervention in the local foreign exchange market. 

 "The intervention by the central banking authority should be selective rather than continuous," it said. 

 "It is therefore recommended that there should be no statutory obligation as it exists today on the RBI to fix its buying and selling rates on a daily basis and instead it should be enabled to intervene only when required in keeping with the objectives of its policy," the committee said. 

 The RBI offers a daily buying and selling rate of 31.37 and 31.53 rupees per dollar to the banks. RBI had been continously present in the market on the buying side until February 1995. 

 "Although this policy has helped to keep the dollar-rupee levels stable, it is market forces which should determine the value of home currency against the foreign currency," the committee said.
